plan.step.description: Line under the title of the read-only plan page for a project's first version: how far the assistant's work on it has come. {{step}} is the current step's number and {{total}} how many steps there are, for example Step 3 of 7.

plan.decides.named.description: Line at the foot of the read-only plan page for a project's first version, telling a member who may approve the plan. {{username}} is the username of the person who started the project.

plan.decides.starter.text: The person who started it decides on this plan.
plan.decides.starter.description: Line at the foot of the read-only plan page for a project's first version, when the name of the person who started the project is not known. "It" is the project.

plan.chosen.named.text: {{username}} chose this plan. Once it’s live, anyone here can suggest changes.
plan.chosen.named.description: Line on the read-only plan page of a project's first version while the plan is being built or tested: its maker already chose it. {{username}} is the maker's username. "Live" means built and running.

plan.chosen.starter.text: The person who started it chose this plan. Once it’s live, anyone here can suggest changes.
plan.chosen.starter.description: Line on the read-only plan page of a project's first version while the plan is being built or tested, when the maker's name is not known. "It" is the project. "Live" means built and running.

plan.backHub.description: Name of the place the back arrow on the read-only plan page returns to: the project's Hub tab. It fills the place in "Back to Hub".

plan.botNameBadge.description: Author's name at the top of the read-only plan page, beside the assistant's picture, with a small badge after it. "Homeroom bot" is the name of Homeroom's assistant, which wrote the plan; keep "Homeroom". <0></0> is the badge marking the author as an AI assistant rather than a person.

plan.title.description: Heading of the read-only plan page. "My" is Homeroom bot, the assistant, speaking: it is the plan the assistant wrote for the project's first version. {{project}} is the project's name.

plan.linesLabel.description: Accessible name of the list of the plan's lines, on the read-only plan page and in the plan sheet a member opens from the App tab while the first version is built. {{project}} is the project's name.

plan.talk.description: Button at the foot of the read-only plan page: opens the project's #general channel so a member can say something about the plan. "#general" is the name of that channel; keep it as written.

discussion.label.description: Accessible name of the Discussion tab's content on a project's page: the project's chat channel. {{project}} is the project's name.

discussion.none.text: This project has no discussion you can read.
discussion.none.description: Shown on a project's Discussion tab in place of the chat when this person is not allowed to read the project's channel.

discussion.closeThread.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the X button on the panel of replies to one message, beside a project's discussion. Close is a verb: it hides the panel of replies.

invite.from.isMaking.text: {{name}} is making it and invited you
invite.from.isMaking.description: First line of a project's page when it was opened from an invite link, above the Join button, while the project's first version is still being built. {{name}} is the display name of the person who started the project and sent the invite; "it" is the project.

invite.from.made.description: First line of a project's page when it was opened from an invite link, above the Join button. {{name}} is the display name of the person who started the project and sent the invite; "it" is the project.

invite.from.invited.description: First line of a project's page when it was opened from an invite link, above the Join button, when the inviter did not start the project. {{username}} is the inviter's username; keep the @ before it.

invite.from.unnamed.description: First line of a project's page when it was opened from an invite link, above the Join button, when who sent the invite is not known.

invite.dead.expired.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the link's time limit ran out in the meantime.

invite.dead.revoked.text: That invite link was turned off.
invite.dead.revoked.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the person who made the link has cancelled it.

invite.dead.usedUp.text: That invite link has been used as many times as it allows.
invite.dead.usedUp.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the link's limit on how many people may use it has been reached.

invite.dead.unknown.text: That invite link does not work.
invite.dead.unknown.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the link is not one Homeroom knows.

invite.previewOnly.text: This is a preview of an invite, so nothing was joined.
invite.previewOnly.description: Toast after pressing Join on a demonstration copy of an invited person's view of a project's page, which follows no real invite link.

invite.joinFailed.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when joining failed for a reason the server did not explain or the request did not get through.

invite.usernameFirst.description: Error toast after pressing Join on a project's page opened from an invite link, when the person has no username yet and a public community requires one. Shown only when the server sent no sentence of its own.

invite.joined.description: Toast shown once a person has joined a community through an invite link.

hub.channel.unread_one.description: Small badge in the head of the Discussion card: how many messages in the project's channel are unread. {{shown}} is that number as displayed, capped as 99+; the plural form follows the real count.

hub.channel.unread_other.description: Small badge in the head of the Discussion card: how many messages in the project's channel are unread. {{shown}} is that number as displayed, capped as 99+; the plural form follows the real count.

hub.channel.sayHi.description: Button on the Discussion card of a project's Hub when nobody has written in the project's channel yet: opens the Discussion tab to write the first message. {{project}} is the project's name.

hub.firstVersion.review.description: Main button on the first-version card of a project's Hub, for the person who started the project: opens their chat with Homeroom bot, where the plan for the first version waits for their go-ahead.

hub.firstVersion.answer.description: Main button on the first-version card of a project's Hub, for the person who started the project: opens their chat with Homeroom bot, which has asked them a question before it can go on building.

hub.firstVersion.tryIt.description: Main button on the first-version card of a project's Hub once the first version is built and up for approval: opens that version so the person can use it before approving. "It" is the app.

hub.firstVersion.openApp.description: Button on the first-version card of a project's Hub once the first version is live. Open is a verb: goes to the running app.

hub.firstVersion.seePlan.description: Quiet link on the first-version card of a project's Hub, for a member who did not start the project: opens the plan for the first version to read, without being able to answer it.

hub.needs.title.description: Heading of the card on a project's Hub that leads to the Needs you tab: the proposals waiting for this person's vote.

hub.needs.toVote_one.description: Beside the heading of the Needs you card on a project's Hub: how many proposals this person has not yet looked at and still has to vote on.

hub.needs.toVote_other.description: Beside the heading of the Needs you card on a project's Hub: how many proposals this person has not yet looked at and still has to vote on.

hub.needs.skipped_one.text: {{count}} vote you skipped is still open
hub.needs.skipped_one.description: Line on the Needs you card of a project's Hub when every proposal waiting for this person's vote is one they already swiped past without voting: how many of those can still be voted on.

hub.needs.skipped_other.text: {{count}} votes you skipped are still open
hub.needs.skipped_other.description: Line on the Needs you card of a project's Hub when every proposal waiting for this person's vote is one they already swiped past without voting: how many of those can still be voted on.

hub.needs.joinToVote.description: Note under the Needs you card of a project's Hub for a person who is not a member of the community: they must join it before they can vote on the proposals. "These" are the proposals.

hub.needs.none.description: Quiet line on a project's Hub, in place of the Needs you card, when no proposal waits for this person's vote.

hub.needs.noneButRequests_one.text: Nothing more to vote on · <0>{{count}} request nobody has picked up</0>
hub.needs.noneButRequests_one.description: Quiet line on a project's Hub, in place of the Needs you card, when no proposal waits for this person's vote but some requests (filed issues) have nobody working on them. The part in <0></0> is a link that opens the Needs you tab. {{count}} is the number of such requests.

hub.needs.noneButRequests_other.text: Nothing more to vote on · <0>{{count}} requests nobody has picked up</0>
hub.needs.noneButRequests_other.description: Quiet line on a project's Hub, in place of the Needs you card, when no proposal waits for this person's vote but some requests (filed issues) have nobody working on them. The part in <0></0> is a link that opens the Needs you tab. {{count}} is the number of such requests.

hub.needs.requestsAlone_one.description: Quiet line on the Hub of a project that has only one person in it, when some requests (filed issues) have nobody working on them. The whole line, inside <0></0>, is a link that opens the Needs you tab. {{count}} is the number of such requests.

hub.needs.requestsAlone_other.description: Quiet line on the Hub of a project that has only one person in it, when some requests (filed issues) have nobody working on them. The whole line, inside <0></0>, is a link that opens the Needs you tab. {{count}} is the number of such requests.

hub.work.title.description: Heading of the card on a project's Hub that lists the changes and requests this person started in the project.

hub.work.empty.description: Shown on the Your work card of a project's Hub when this person has nothing under way in the project.

hub.work.emptyBot.text: Nothing in progress. To change something, tell Homeroom bot.
hub.work.emptyBot.description: Shown on the Your work card of a project's Hub when the person is alone in the project, has nothing under way, and Homeroom bot builds changes for them there. "Homeroom bot" is the assistant's name and stays as it is.

hub.work.emptyMenu.text: Nothing in progress. Press <0>⋯</0> to suggest an improvement.
hub.work.emptyMenu.description: Shown on the Your work card of a project's Hub when the person is alone in the project and has nothing under way. The ⋯ in <0></0> is the three-dot menu button on the same page, shown in the accent colour; keep the symbol.

hub.people.active_one.description: Top of a project's Hub, beside the faces of the people active there: how many people took part in the project in the last seven days (talked in its channel, started a change or voted).

hub.people.active_other.description: Top of a project's Hub, beside the faces of the people active there: how many people took part in the project in the last seven days (talked in its channel, started a change or voted).

hub.people.namesAndMore_one.description: Line under "40 active this week" at the top of a project's Hub. {{names}} is a list of up to five usernames of people active this week, already joined with commas; {{count}} is how many more people were active who are not named.

hub.people.namesAndMore_other.description: Line under "40 active this week" at the top of a project's Hub. {{names}} is a list of up to five usernames of people active this week, already joined with commas; {{count}} is how many more people were active who are not named.

hub.people.moreFaces_one.description: Last circle in the row of faces at the top of a project's Hub: how many more people were active this week than the faces shown. Keep it as short as a plus sign and a number.

hub.people.moreFaces_other.description: Last circle in the row of faces at the top of a project's Hub: how many more people were active this week than the faces shown. Keep it as short as a plus sign and a number.

hub.forYou.title.description: Small heading over the card of what on a project is this person's: the votes they owe, their own work and the project's discussion, on the project's Hub.

hub.forYou.needs.firstAndMore_one.description: Second line of the Needs you row on a project's Hub: the title of the first change waiting on this person's vote, then how many more are waiting. {{title}} is that change's title.

hub.forYou.needs.firstAndMore_other.description: Second line of the Needs you row on a project's Hub: the title of the first change waiting on this person's vote, then how many more are waiting. {{title}} is that change's title.

hub.forYou.work.inProgress_one.description: Right end of the Your work row on a project's Hub: how many of this person's own requests and changes are in flight in the project.

hub.forYou.work.inProgress_other.description: Right end of the Your work row on a project's Hub: how many of this person's own requests and changes are in flight in the project.

hub.forYou.discussion.title.description: Title of the row that opens a project's discussion on its Hub. <0></0> draws the channel's name in a lighter weight; {{handle}} is the channel's name without the #, for example general.

hub.forYou.discussion.lastBy.description: Second line of the Discussion row on a project's Hub: the last message in the channel, who wrote it and how long ago. {{username}} is the writer, {{message}} the message itself, {{ago}} a time such as "4h ago".

hub.forYou.discussion.last.description: Second line of the Discussion row on a project's Hub when the last message in the channel has no writer to name: the message and how long ago it was sent. {{ago}} is a time such as "4h ago".

hub.forYou.discussion.postedBy.description: Second line of the Discussion row on a project's Hub when the newest message in the channel has no words to quote (only a picture or a file): who sent it and how long ago. {{ago}} is a time such as "4h ago".

hub.forYou.discussion.posted.description: Second line of the Discussion row on a project's Hub when the newest message in the channel has no words to quote and no writer to name: how long ago it was sent. {{ago}} is a time such as "4h ago".

hub.recent.title.description: Small heading over the cards of the last few changes that went live, on a project's Hub.

hub.recent.all.description: Link beside the Recently live heading on a project's Hub: opens the project's Workshop, where everything that went live is listed week by week.

hub.recent.byAgo.description: Line under a change's title in Recently live on a project's Hub: who made the change and how long ago it went live. {{who}} is a username or "Homeroom bot"; {{ago}} a time such as "1h ago".

hub.recent.byGoing.description: Line under a change's title in Recently live on a project's Hub, for a change that has merged and is still on its way to the live app. {{who}} is a username or "Homeroom bot".

communityCard.audience.justYou.description: Name of the audience of a project only its maker is in, used as the project's audience line when the server sent no label. It is one of the three audience names, beside Private community and Public community.

communityCard.audience.justYouSoFar.description: Who a project is for, shown at the top of its Hub to the one person in it while nobody else has joined, with an Invite button beside it. "Just you" is the name of that audience (beside Private community and Public community); "so far" says it can grow.

communityCard.audience.withMembers_one.description: One-line summary of who a project is for and how many people are in it. {{audience}} is the audience's name, already in the reader's language: Private community or Public community. {{count}} is the number of members.

communityCard.audience.withMembers_other.description: One-line summary of who a project is for and how many people are in it. {{audience}} is the audience's name, already in the reader's language: Private community or Public community. {{count}} is the number of members.

communityCard.audienceChange.toPublic.text: Making it a public community is waiting for approval

communityCard.audienceChange.toPrivate.text: Making it a private community is waiting for approval

communityCard.audienceChange.other.text: A change to who it is for is waiting for approval

communityCard.audienceChange.failed.text: That did not go through. Try again.
communityCard.audienceChange.failed.description: Error shown when proposing to make a project public or private failed and the server gave no reason of its own: as a toast after the confirm dialog, or under the question in the Make it public popup.

communityCard.week.privateCommunity.description: Audience name shown in bold beside the faces at the top of a project's Hub in its first week, when the project is still just its maker's but an invite link has been sent out. One of the three audience names.

communityCard.week.people_other.description: Small line under the audience name at the top of a project's Hub in its first week: how many people are in the community.

communityCard.makePublic.question.description: Question asked before proposing to make a private project public: the title of the confirm dialog from the project's ⋯ menu, and the question in the popup under the "Make it public" button. {{project}} is the project's name.

communityCard.makePublic.explain.text: Anyone can find it on Discover, join, and propose changes. Members vote on this first, and it applies once it merges.
communityCard.makePublic.explain.description: Explanation under the question "Make {{project}} a public community?". "It" is the project; Discover is the name of the screen for finding apps and communities. "This" is the proposal to make it public, which is put to a vote and takes effect once it is merged.

communityCard.makePublic.propose.description: Confirming button under the question "Make {{project}} a public community?": puts the change up as a proposal for the members to vote on. "It" is the project.

communityCard.makePublic.notNow.description: Declining button under the question "Make {{project}} a public community?": closes it and leaves the project as it is.

communityCard.share.title.description: Heading of a card at the foot of the Hub of a project only its maker is in, offering to invite people or make it public. Share is a verb; "it" is the project.

communityCard.share.line.text: Invite people to make it a private community, or make it public so anyone can join.
communityCard.share.line.description: Text of the "Share it" card on the Hub of a project only its maker is in, above the Invite people and Make it public buttons. "It" is the project.

communityCard.share.lineBuilding.text: Invite people to follow along while it’s being built, or make it public so anyone can join.
communityCard.share.lineBuilding.description: Text of the "Share it" card on the Hub of a project only its maker is in, while Homeroom bot is still building the project's first version. "It" is the project.

communityCard.share.invite.description: Button on the "Share it" card: opens the pane that makes an invite link to the project.

communityCard.share.makePublic.description: Button on the "Share it" card: opens a small popup asking whether to propose making the project a public community. "It" is the project.

communityCard.inviteCard.note.description: The inviter's personal note, shown in quotation marks under the line saying who invited the person, on a project's page opened from an invite link. {{note}} is text the inviter wrote; only the quotation marks are translated.

communityCard.inviteCard.join.description: Large main button at the top of a project's page opened from an invite link, and on the preview of a private community's invite: joins the community through that link. {{project}} is the project's name.

communityCard.inviteCard.joinUnnamed.description: Large main button at the top of a project's page opened from an invite link, and on the preview of a private community's invite: joins the community through that link. Used when the community's name did not come with the link.

communityCard.join.button.description: Button in the action row at the top of a project's Hub, for a person who is not a member: opens a small popup asking whether to join the community.

communityCard.join.question.description: Question in the small popup under the Join button at the top of a project's Hub, and that popup's accessible name. {{project}} is the project's name.

communityCard.join.explain.text: Members start changes, file requests, vote and chat here.
communityCard.join.explain.description: Explanation under the question "Join {{project}}?": what a member of the community can do in the project. Changes are proposed changes to the project; requests are filed issues.

communityCard.join.answer.description: Confirming button under the question "Join {{project}}?": makes the person a member of the community.

communityCard.join.notNow.description: Declining button under the question "Join {{project}}?": closes the popup without joining.

communityCard.openApp.description: Button in the action row at the top of a project's Hub, after a play icon. Open is a verb: goes to the running app.

communityCard.invite.button.description: Button in the action row at the top of a project's Hub, for a member. A verb: opens the pane that makes an invite link to the community.

communityCard.invite.title.description: Tooltip of the Invite button in the action row at the top of a project's Hub.

topic.frame.resizeSpecPanel.description: Accessible name of the draggable divider between a proposal's or request's page and the plan reader docked beside it. A plan is the written description a change is built from.

topic.back.messages.description: Text of the back chip at the top of a proposal's or request's page when it was opened from a conversation: the name of the Messages screen it returns to. Shown after a left-pointing chevron.

topic.back.workshop.description: Text of the back chip at the top of a proposal's or request's page: the name of the project's Workshop tab (the build tab beside its Hub) that the chip returns to. A noun, shown after a left-pointing chevron.

topic.back.toMessages.description: Accessible name of the back chip on a proposal's or request's page that was opened from a conversation. Messages is the screen of the person's conversations.

topic.back.toWorkshop.description: Accessible name of the back chip on a proposal's or request's page. Workshop is the project's build tab, where its proposals and requests are listed.

topic.editor.title.description: Heading of the dialog where the author of a change rewrites the description people read before voting on it.

topic.editor.closeLabel.description: Accessible name of the X button that closes the edit-description dialog of a change without saving.

topic.editor.help.text: Explain the problem and what this change does. Markdown is supported.
topic.editor.help.description: Help line under the heading of the edit-description dialog of a change. Markdown is the name of a text formatting syntax; do not translate it.

topic.editor.loading.description: Status line in the edit-description dialog of a change while the current description is being fetched.

topic.editor.fieldLabel.description: Label of the large text field in the edit-description dialog of a change. A noun: the text describing the change.

topic.editor.previewRegion.description: Accessible name of the area that shows the formatted description, in the edit-description dialog of a change, while Preview is on.

topic.editor.preview.description: Toggle button in the edit-description dialog of a change: shows the description as it will look once formatted, in place of the text field. A verb.

topic.editor.editText.description: Toggle button in the edit-description dialog of a change, shown while the formatted preview is on: goes back to the text field.

topic.editor.tooLong.text: Shorten the description before saving; none of your text has been removed.
topic.editor.tooLong.description: Alert in the edit-description dialog of a change when the text is over the length limit. Saving is disabled until it is shorter.

topic.editor.loadFailed.description: Error in the edit-description dialog of a change when the current description could not be fetched and the server gave no message of its own.

topic.editor.saveFailed.description: Error in the edit-description dialog of a change when saving was refused and the server gave no message of its own.

topic.editor.connectFailed.text: Could not connect. Your draft is kept; try saving again.
topic.editor.connectFailed.description: Error in the edit-description dialog of a change when the save request could not reach the server. The text the person typed is still in the field.

topic.editor.savedSyncIncomplete.text: Saved in Homeroom. Pull-request synchronization is incomplete. Save again to retry.
topic.editor.savedSyncIncomplete.description: Status line in the edit-description dialog of a change: the description was saved, but copying it to the change's pull request on GitHub failed. Homeroom is the product's name.

topic.editor.savedToast.description: Brief confirmation shown after the edit-description dialog of a change saved and closed.

topic.editor.reviewLatest.description: Button in the edit-description dialog of a change, shown when someone else saved a newer description while the person was editing: loads that newer text so the two can be compared.

topic.editor.latestTitle.description: Heading over the newer description somebody else saved, shown in the edit-description dialog of a change after a save conflict.

topic.editor.useLatest.description: Button under the newer description in the edit-description dialog of a change: replaces the person's draft with that newer saved text.

topic.editor.keepDraft.description: Button under the newer description in the edit-description dialog of a change: keeps what the person typed, so saving will overwrite the newer saved text.

topic.editor.save.description: Main button of the edit-description dialog of a change: saves the text as the change's description.

topic.editor.saving.description: Text of the main button in the edit-description dialog of a change while the description is being saved.

topic.editor.retrySync.description: Text of the main button in the edit-description dialog of a change after the description was saved but could not be copied to its pull request on GitHub: saves again to retry that copy. GitHub is a product name.

topic.check.advisory.description: Small lower-case tag on one automated check in a change's list of checks: this check's result is shown for information and does not block the change from going live.

topic.check.flaky.description: Small lower-case tag on one automated check in a change's list of checks: the check fails intermittently. {{percent}} is the share of its recorded runs that failed. Keep the dot and the percent sign.

topic.check.flakyTitle.text: Failed about {{percent}}% of its recorded runs
topic.check.flakyTitle.description: Hover text of the "flaky" tag on an automated check. {{percent}} is the share of that check's recorded runs that failed.

topic.check.whyItFailed.description: Link-like label at the right end of a failed automated check's row on a change's page: opens the reason the check failed. "It" is the check.

topic.check.passedOnRetry.description: Link-like label at the right end of an automated check's row on a change's page, for a check that failed once and passed when run again: opens the reason of the first failure.

topic.check.failed.description: Lower-case word shown as the reason of a failed automated check when the run recorded no reason. Describes the check.

topic.check.reasonOnPath.description: The opened reason of a failed automated check, followed by the page it ran on. {{reason}} is the recorded reason, or the word for "failed"; {{path}} is the address of the page inside the app, for example /settings. <0></0> dims the second part; keep the dot and the space before it inside the tag.

topic.check.testInFile.description: One failing unit test listed under a failed check on a change's page. {{test}} is the test's name and {{file}} the source file it is in. <0></0> and <1></1> style the two parts; keep the dot and the space before it inside the second tag.

topic.checks.showPassing_one.description: Label that unfolds the list of automated checks that passed, in the checks box under a proposal. {{count}} is how many passed.

topic.checks.showPassing_other.description: Label that unfolds the list of automated checks that passed, in the checks box under a proposal. {{count}} is how many passed.

topic.checks.passNamesLoading.description: Line inside the unfolded list of passed automated checks on a change's page while their names are being fetched.

topic.checks.passNamesFailed.text: Could not load the passing checks. Close this and open it again to retry.
topic.checks.passNamesFailed.description: Line inside the unfolded list of passed automated checks on a change's page when their names could not be fetched. "This" is the fold the person just opened.

topic.ledger.passing_one.description: Small button on the checks row of a change's page that unfolds the automated checks that passed. {{count}} is how many passed.

topic.ledger.passing_other.description: Small button on the checks row of a change's page that unfolds the automated checks that passed. {{count}} is how many passed.

topic.build.seconds.description: How long one step of a change's preview build took, when under a minute, shown small after the step's name. {{seconds}} is a whole number; "s" abbreviates seconds.

topic.build.minutesSeconds.description: How long one step of a change's preview build took, when a minute or more, shown small after the step's name. {{minutes}} and {{seconds}} are whole numbers; "m" and "s" abbreviate minutes and seconds.

topic.roster.loading.description: Shown on the votes line of a proposal's page while the list of who voted is being fetched.

topic.roster.approved.description: The votes line of a proposal that has the Yes votes it needs, when no voter can be named. Describes the proposal.

topic.roster.approvedBy.description: The votes line of a proposal that has the Yes votes it needs. {{approvers}} is the list of people who voted Yes, already joined, for example "@maya ✓, @sam". <0></0> shows the first word bold in green.

topic.roster.approvedByWithNo.description: The votes line of a proposal that has the Yes votes it needs although some people voted No. {{approvers}} is the list of people who voted Yes and {{against}} the list who voted No, each already joined. <0></0> shows the first word bold in green; <1></1> dims the No part: keep the dot and the space before it inside that tag. "No" is the name of the vote against.

topic.roster.approvedWithNo.description: The votes line of a proposal that has the Yes votes it needs, when only the people who voted No can be named. {{against}} is that list, already joined. <0></0> shows the first word bold in green; <1></1> dims the No part: keep the dot and the space before it inside that tag.

topic.roster.waiting.description: The votes line of a proposal that does not yet have the votes it needs, when nobody has voted either way.

topic.roster.waitingYes.description: The votes line of a proposal that does not yet have the votes it needs, when only Yes votes were cast. {{yesLabel}} is the Yes side's label with its count, for example "Yes (2)", and {{yesNames}} the people who voted Yes, already joined. <0></0> shows the opening sentence bold: keep the space at its end inside the tag. <1></1> colours the label.

topic.roster.waitingYesNo.description: The votes line of a proposal that does not yet have the votes it needs, when people voted both ways. {{yesLabel}} and {{noLabel}} are each side's label with its count, for example "Yes (2)" and "No (1)"; {{yesNames}} and {{noNames}} are the people on each side, already joined. <0></0> shows the opening sentence bold: keep the space at its end inside the tag. <1></1> and <2></2> colour the two labels.

topic.roster.waitingNo.description: The votes line of a proposal that does not yet have the votes it needs, when only No votes were cast. {{noLabel}} is the No side's label with its count, for example "No (1)", and {{noNames}} the people who voted No, already joined. <0></0> shows the opening sentence bold: keep the space at its end inside the tag. <2></2> colours the label; keep its number.

topic.roster.reason.description: One line under a proposal's votes: a voter and the sentence they wrote with their vote, quoted. {{voter}} is the person's @name and {{reason}} their own words. Use the quotation marks of the language.

topic.help.howVotingWorks.description: Link at the right end of the votes line on a proposal's page: opens a short explanation of how proposals are voted on and go live.

topic.help.votingAndMerges.description: Accessible name and hover text of the round "?" button beside "How voting works" on a proposal's page: opens the same explanation. A merge is an approved change going into the project's code.

topic.steps.votingHelp.description: Accessible name and hover text of the round "?" button on the Votes step of a proposal's list of steps: opens a short explanation of voting. A merge is an approved change going into the project's code.

topic.steps.voteTally.description: The count of votes on the Votes step of a proposal. {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes and {{no}} the number of No votes. Yes and No are the names of the two votes.

topic.about.title.description: Heading of the section under a proposal's or request's card that holds its description, used when the page gave no more specific heading. A noun-like heading, as in "About this change".

topic.about.whatChanges.description: Sub-heading over the plain-language summary of a proposal: what people using the app will notice once the change is live.

topic.about.technicalDetails.description: Label that unfolds the full technical description of a proposal (its pull-request text), under the plain-language summary.

topic.about.testing.title.description: Label that unfolds the instructions for trying a proposal out before voting on it.

topic.about.testing.recordedIn.description: Shown under "Testing instructions" on a proposal when the instructions exist only as a file in the project's code. {{path}} is that file's path.

topic.about.testing.none.text: No testing instructions have been added yet.
topic.about.testing.none.description: Shown under "Testing instructions" on a proposal that has none.

topic.hero.howItsBuilt.description: Label that unfolds the technical design part of a change's summary on the change's page, under the part written for the people deciding on it. "It" is the change.

topic.transcript.readOnly.description: Small lower-case tag on the fold that shows the chat in which a change was built: the chat can be read here but not continued.

topic.change.refreshFailed.description: Error at the top of a change's page when re-reading its current state failed and the server gave no message of its own. A Retry button follows it.

topic.change.includedInRegion.text: The change this one went live in
topic.change.includedInRegion.description: Accessible name of the box on a change's page that links to the later change it was merged as part of. "This one" is the change being viewed.

topic.change.sheetLabel.description: Accessible name of the sheet that holds a change's page. A noun: a change to the project that is being built or voted on.

topic.change.bar.titleNumbered.description: Title in the header of a change's page. {{number}} is the change's number. "Change" is a noun: a change to the project that is being built or voted on.

topic.change.bar.title.description: Title in the header of a change's page while the change has no number yet. A noun: a change to the project that is being built.

topic.change.bar.more.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the ⋯ button in the header of a change's page: opens the menu with everything else that can be done with the change.

topic.change.summaryStale.text: Written for an earlier version of this change.
topic.change.summaryStale.description: Note under a change's summary on its page when the change was updated after the summary was written, so the summary may no longer describe it.

topic.change.gate.noteSeeFailed.description: The line under the Testing card on a change's page when its checks failed. {{note}} is one or more whole sentences, already worded, saying what happened. <0></0> is a link-style button that opens the Details sheet at the failed checks.

topic.change.gate.seeFailed.description: Link-style button under the Testing card on a change's page when its checks failed and there is nothing else to say: opens the Details sheet at the failed checks.

topic.change.shots.title.description: Name, and accessible name, of the card on a change's page that holds screenshots of the app before and after the change, or the line saying where they are.

topic.change.stream.replies_one.description: Line under a change, over the replies to it, on the change's page: how many replies people have written. {{count}} is that number. Reply is a noun.

topic.change.stream.replies_other.description: Line under a change, over the replies to it, on the change's page: how many replies people have written. {{count}} is that number. Reply is a noun.

topic.change.stream.noReplies.description: Line under a change, on its page, when nobody has replied to it.

topic.change.stream.loading.description: Line under a change, on its page, while the replies to it are being fetched.

topic.change.stream.loadEarlier.description: Button at the top of the replies on a change's page: fetches the older replies before the ones shown. Load is a verb.

topic.change.stream.tryIt.description: Link-style button at the end of the line "The preview is ready" among the replies on a change's page: opens the preview so the person can use the change before voting. "It" is the change.

topic.change.line.postedSpec.description: One line among the replies on a change's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description the change is built from) was posted. {{author}} is who posted it, a username, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version.

topic.change.line.postedSpecUnnamed.description: One line among the replies on a change's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description the change is built from) was posted. Used when nobody can be named; "Someone" is written as the line has always shown it. {{version}} is the plan's version number.

topic.change.line.previewReady.description: One line among the replies on a change's page, saying something that happened: the preview build of the change finished and can be opened. A "Try it" button follows it. No full stop.

topic.change.line.askedForApproval.description: One line among the replies on a change's page, saying something that happened: the change was put up for the members' vote. {{author}} is the username of who did it, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.change.line.unnamedAskedForApprova.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: the change was put up for the members' vote, when it is not known by whom. A past-tense verb phrase with no subject.

topic.change.line.votedYes.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted in favour of the change. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.change.line.votedYesReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted in favour of the change and gave a reason. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{reason}} is what they wrote, in their own words; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>.

topic.change.line.votedYesEarlier.text: <0>{{voter}}</0> voted yes on an earlier version
topic.change.line.votedYesEarlier.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted in favour, but the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.change.line.votedYesEarlierReason.text: <0>{{voter}}</0> voted yes on an earlier version<1>: “{{reason}}”</1>
topic.change.line.votedYesEarlierReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted in favour and gave a reason, but the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>.

topic.change.line.votedNo.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted against the change. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.change.line.votedNoReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted against the change and gave a reason. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{reason}} is what they wrote, in their own words; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>.

topic.change.line.votedNoEarlier.text: <0>{{voter}}</0> voted no on an earlier version
topic.change.line.votedNoEarlier.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted against, but the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.change.line.votedNoEarlierReason.text: <0>{{voter}}</0> voted no on an earlier version<1>: “{{reason}}”</1>
topic.change.line.votedNoEarlierReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: a member voted against and gave a reason, but the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts. {{voter}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYes.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted in favour of the change, when it is not known who. A past-tense verb phrase with no subject.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYesReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted in favour of the change and gave a reason, when it is not known who. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>. There is no <0> tag in this line.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYesEarlier.text: Voted yes on an earlier version
topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYesEarlier.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted in favour, when it is not known who, and the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYesEarlier.text: Voted yes on an earlier version<1>: “{{reason}}”</1>
topic.change.line.unnamedVotedYesEarlier.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted in favour and gave a reason, when it is not known who, and the change has been updated since. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>. There is no <0> tag in this line.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNo.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted against the change, when it is not known who. A past-tense verb phrase with no subject.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNoReason.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted against the change and gave a reason, when it is not known who. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>. There is no <0> tag in this line.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNoEarlier.text: Voted no on an earlier version
topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNoEarlier.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted against, when it is not known who, and the change has been updated since, so that vote no longer counts.

topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNoEarlierR.text: Voted no on an earlier version<1>: “{{reason}}”</1>
topic.change.line.unnamedVotedNoEarlierR.description: One line among the replies on a change's page: somebody voted against and gave a reason, when it is not known who, and the change has been updated since. {{reason}} is what they wrote; keep it and its quotation marks inside <1></1>. There is no <0> tag in this line.

topic.requests.region.description: Accessible name of the row on a change's page, under its summary, that names the requests (filed issues) the change is meant to resolve.

topic.requests.addresses.description: Label at the start of the row on a change's page that names the requests it resolves: the first request follows it as a chip, with a "+N more" button when there are others. A verb in the third person: this change addresses these requests. Not postal addresses.

topic.requests.more_one.description: Button after the first request on the "Addresses" row of a change's page, when the change resolves more than one request: shows the others, one to a line. {{count}} is how many others there are. Keep the plus sign.

topic.requests.more_other.description: Button after the first request on the "Addresses" row of a change's page, when the change resolves more than one request: shows the others, one to a line. {{count}} is how many others there are. Keep the plus sign.

topic.requests.showLess.description: Replaces the "+N more" button on the "Addresses" row of a change's page while the other requests are shown: hides them again.

topic.requests.selectedCount_one.description: Small heading over the requests currently linked, in the editor of a change's linked requests. {{count}} is how many are selected.

topic.requests.selectedCount_other.description: Small heading over the requests currently linked, in the editor of a change's linked requests. {{count}} is how many are selected.

topic.requests.remaining_one.description: Shown opposite "Selected" in the editor of a change's linked requests: how many more requests may still be linked before the limit. {{count}} is that number.

topic.requests.remaining_other.description: Shown opposite "Selected" in the editor of a change's linked requests: how many more requests may still be linked before the limit. {{count}} is that number.

topic.requests.remove.description: Accessible name of the X button on one selected request in the editor of a change's linked requests: unlinks it. {{number}} is the request's number and {{title}} its title. Keep the # sign.

topic.requests.noneSelected.description: Shown under "Selected" in the editor of a change's linked requests when none is selected.

topic.requests.addAnother.description: Label of the search field in the editor of a change's linked requests: finds an existing request (filed issue) to link.

topic.requests.searchPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the search field in the editor of a change's linked requests. A request can be found by its number or by words in its title.

topic.requests.matches.description: Accessible name of the list of search results under the search field in the editor of a change's linked requests.

topic.requests.addNamed.description: Accessible name of one search result in the editor of a change's linked requests: selecting it links that request. {{number}} is the request's number and {{title}} its title. Keep the # sign.

topic.requests.addNumbered.description: Accessible name of the search result that links a request by the exact number the person typed, when its title is not known. {{number}} is that number. Keep the # sign.

topic.requests.addByNumber.description: Text of the search result that links a request by the exact number the person typed, shown where a request's title would be. "Issue" is another word for a request here.

topic.requests.untitled.description: Stand-in title for a selected request whose real title is not known, in the editor of a change's linked requests. {{number}} is the request's number. Keep the # sign.

topic.requests.noMatches.text: No matching open requests. Enter a request number to add it.
topic.requests.noMatches.description: Shown under the search field in the editor of a change's linked requests when nothing matches what was typed.

topic.requests.searchHelp.text: Searches open requests in this project. You can always add one by its number.
topic.requests.searchHelp.description: Help line under the search field in the editor of a change's linked requests. Open requests are the ones not yet closed.

topic.requests.numberTooLarge.text: “{{input}}” is too large to be an issue number.
topic.requests.numberTooLarge.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when the number typed is too big to be a request's number. {{input}} is exactly what the person typed. "Issue" is another word for a request here.

topic.requests.chooseOrEnter.text: Choose a matching issue or enter its issue number.
topic.requests.chooseOrEnter.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when Enter is pressed and the text typed matches no request and is not a number. "Issue" is another word for a request here.

topic.requests.tooMany_one.text: A change can link at most {{count}} requests.
topic.requests.tooMany_one.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when the limit is reached. {{count}} is the largest number of requests one change may be linked to.

topic.requests.tooMany_other.text: A change can link at most {{count}} requests.
topic.requests.tooMany_other.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when the limit is reached. {{count}} is the largest number of requests one change may be linked to.

topic.requests.updateFailed.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when saving was refused and the server gave no message of its own.

topic.requests.networkError.description: Error in the editor of a change's linked requests when the save request could not reach the server.

topic.requests.saved.description: Confirmation under the "Addresses" line of a change after its linked requests were saved. "Issues" is another word for requests here.

topic.requests.savedSyncPending.text: Issues saved. The pull request could not be updated yet; saving again will retry it.
topic.requests.savedSyncPending.description: Confirmation under the "Addresses" line of a change after its linked requests were saved in Homeroom but could not be written to the change's pull request on GitHub. "Issues" is another word for requests here.

topic.requests.save.description: Main button of the editor of a change's linked requests: saves which requests the change is linked to. "Requests" is a noun here.

topic.requests.saving.description: Text of the main button in the editor of a change's linked requests while the links are being saved.

topic.request.addressedByRegion.description: Accessible name of the box on a request's page that links to the change being built or voted on to resolve it. "Issue" is another word for the request.

topic.request.closedBand.closed.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when neither the date nor the way it was closed is known. "Closed" is an adjective describing the request, not the verb for closing a window. <0></0> draws it bold.

topic.request.closedBand.when.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when only the date is known. "Closed" is an adjective describing the request. {{date}} is a short date or relative time, for example Oct 5 or 3d ago. <0></0> is the status word, drawn bold; <1></1> is a separator dot hidden from screen readers; <2></2> holds the date. Keep every tag, in the order your language reads.

topic.request.closedBand.whenByChange.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when a merged change closed it: closed, on this date, by this change. {{date}} is a short date or relative time, for example Oct 5 or 3d ago. <0></0> is the status word, drawn bold; <1></1> and <3></3> are separator dots hidden from screen readers; <2></2> holds the date; <4></4> holds the word that introduces the change; <5></5> is a link showing the change's number and title, which fills itself in: leave it empty and put it where the change's name belongs.

topic.request.closedBand.byChange.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when a merged change closed it and the date is not known: closed by this change. <0></0> is the status word, drawn bold; <1></1> is a separator dot hidden from screen readers; <2></2> holds the word that introduces the change; <3></3> is a link showing the change's number and title, which fills itself in: leave it empty and put it where the change's name belongs.

topic.request.closedBand.byChangeLabel.description: Accessible name of the link, in the band at the top of a closed request, to the change that closed it. {{change}} is the change's reference, for example #10, and {{title}} its title.

topic.request.body.title.description: Heading over the description of a request (a filed issue) on its page.

topic.request.body.editTitle.text: Edit this request (you asked for it)
topic.request.body.editTitle.description: Hover text of the pencil button beside "About this request", shown only to the person who filed the request. "You asked for it" means: you are the one who made this request.

topic.request.body.editLabel.description: Accessible name of the pencil button beside "About this request": lets the person who filed the request rewrite its description. A verb phrase.

topic.request.body.empty.description: Shown to the person who filed a request, on its page, when the request has no description.

topic.request.body.unavailable.text: This request is not available right now.
topic.request.body.unavailable.description: Error under the editor of a request's words, on the request's page and in its About sheet, when the edit cannot be saved because the request's project is not loaded.

topic.request.body.saveFailed.description: Error under the editor of a request's words, on the request's page and in its About sheet, when saving failed and the server gave no message of its own.

topic.request.body.save.description: Main button under the description editor of a request: saves the edited description. "Body" is the main text of the request.

topic.request.body.saving.description: Text of the main button under the description editor of a request while the description is being saved.

topic.request.sheetLabel.description: Accessible name of the sheet that holds a request's page. A noun: something a member asked to have built or fixed in the project.

topic.request.bar.title.description: Title in the header of a request's page. {{number}} is the request's number. "Request" is a noun: something a member asked to have built or fixed.

topic.request.bar.more.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the ⋯ button in the header of a request's page: opens the menu with everything else that can be done with the request.

topic.request.words.showMore.description: Button under a request's own words on its page, and under a change's summary on a change's page, while the text is folded after four lines: unfolds all of it.

topic.request.words.showLess.description: Button under a request's own words on its page, and under a change's summary on a change's page, once the text is unfolded: folds it back to four lines.

topic.request.editor.label.description: Accessible name of the text box in which the person who filed a request rewrites its words, on the request's page. A noun.

topic.request.editor.saving.description: Replaces "Save" on the button under the editor of a request's words, on the request's page, while the edit is being saved.

topic.request.status.label.description: Accessible name of the card on a request's page that shows how far the request has come: asked, plan written, built, voted in.

topic.request.status.specVersionReady.text: Plan v{{version}} is ready for comments.
topic.request.status.specVersionReady.description: Sentence in the status card on a request's page once a plan (the written description of the change that would answer the request) has been posted. {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version.

topic.request.status.specReady.text: A plan is ready for comments.
topic.request.status.specReady.description: Sentence in the status card on a request's page once a plan (the written description of the change that would answer the request) has been posted and its version is not known.

topic.request.stage.asked.description: First of the four stops on the progress line of a request's page (Asked, Plan, Built, Voted in): somebody asked for this. A past participle describing the request.

topic.request.stage.spec.description: Second of the four stops on the progress line of a request's page (Asked, Plan, Built, Voted in): a plan, the written description of the change that would answer the request, has been posted. A noun.

topic.request.stage.built.description: Third of the four stops on the progress line of a request's page (Asked, Plan, Built, Voted in): a change that answers the request has been built. A past participle describing the request.

topic.request.stage.voted.description: Last of the four stops on the progress line of a request's page (Asked, Plan, Built, Voted in): the change that answers the request was approved by the members' vote and went live.

topic.request.spec.kicker.description: Small upper-case label over the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan), when the plan has no version number. A noun: the written description the change is built from.

topic.request.spec.kickerVersion.description: Small upper-case label over the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan). "Plan" is a noun: the written description the change is built from. {{version}} is its version number; "v" abbreviates version.

topic.request.spec.by.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan), when the time is not known: who posted the plan. {{author}} is a username, or the assistant's name, Homeroom bot.

topic.request.spec.bySystem.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan), when the time is not known: who posted the plan. Used when the row came with no author and shows "System" in the author's place.

topic.request.spec.bySomeone.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan), when the time is not known: who posted the plan. Used when nobody can be named; "Someone" is written as the line has always shown it.

topic.request.spec.byAt.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan): who posted the plan, and when. {{author}} is a username, or the assistant's name, Homeroom bot. {{time}} is when, already formatted, for example 2:41 PM or Oct 5; keep it inside <0></0>.

topic.request.spec.bySystemAt.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan): who posted the plan, and when. Used when the row came with no author and shows "System" in the author's place. {{time}} is when, already worded.

topic.request.spec.bySomeoneAt.description: Line under the title on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan): who posted the plan, and when. Used when nobody can be named; "Someone" is written as the line has always shown it. {{time}} is when, already formatted.

topic.request.spec.read.description: Button on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan): opens the plan to read beside the page. A verb in the imperative, not the past tense.

topic.request.spec.readNamed.description: Accessible name of the Read button on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan). {{title}} is the plan's title. Read is a verb in the imperative.

topic.request.spec.opening.description: Replaces "Read" on a plan's card (under a request, or on the page of a change built from the plan) while the plan is being fetched.

topic.request.spec.untitled.description: Stands in for the title of a plan that has none, on its card under a request and at the top of the reader that opens it. The plan is the written description of the change that Homeroom's assistant posted on the request's GitHub issue.

topic.request.stream.replies_one.description: Line under a request, over the replies to it, on the request's page: how many replies people have written. {{count}} is that number. Reply is a noun.

topic.request.stream.replies_other.description: Line under a request, over the replies to it, on the request's page: how many replies people have written. {{count}} is that number. Reply is a noun.

topic.request.stream.noReplies.description: Line under a request, on its page, when nobody has replied to it.

topic.request.stream.loading.description: Line under a request, on its page, while the replies to it are being fetched.

topic.request.stream.loadEarlier.description: Button at the top of the replies on a request's page: fetches the older replies before the ones shown. Load is a verb.

topic.request.stream.earlierOnGitHub.text: Earlier GitHub comments aren’t shown here. <0>Read them on GitHub</0>
topic.request.stream.earlierOnGitHub.description: Line at the top of the replies on a request's page when only the newest comments from the request's GitHub issue were fetched. <0></0> is a link to the issue on GitHub, where the rest can be read. GitHub is a product name.

topic.request.stream.earlierNotShown.text: Earlier GitHub comments aren’t shown here.
topic.request.stream.earlierNotShown.description: Line at the top of the replies on a request's page when only the newest comments from the request's GitHub issue were fetched and the issue's address is not known. GitHub is a product name.

topic.request.stream.timeOnGitHub.description: Beside the author's name on a reply, on a request's page, that was written as a comment on the request's GitHub issue rather than in Homeroom. {{time}} is when it was written, already formatted; <0></0> holds it and <1></1> holds the note saying where it was written. Keep both tags. GitHub is a product name.

topic.request.stream.onGitHub.description: Beside the author's name on a reply, on a request's page, that was written as a comment on the request's GitHub issue rather than in Homeroom, when its time is not known. Lower case: it follows the name. GitHub is a product name.

topic.request.stream.postedSpecVersion.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description of the change) was posted. {{author}} is the username of who posted it, drawn bold by <0></0>. {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version.

topic.request.stream.postedSpecVersionUn.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description of the change) was posted. Used when nobody can be named; "Someone" is written as the line has always shown it. {{version}} is the plan's version number.

topic.request.stream.postedSpec.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description of the change) was posted on the request's GitHub issue. {{author}} is who posted it, a username or the assistant's name, Homeroom bot, drawn bold by <0></0>.

topic.request.stream.postedSpecSystem.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a plan (the written description of the change) was posted on the request's GitHub issue. Used when the row came with no author and shows "System" in the author's place. Keep the <0> tag around the word.

topic.request.stream.claimed.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a member took the request on. {{member}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. "This" is the request.

topic.request.stream.claimedPlain.description: Plain-text form of the line saying a member took a request on, for places that show a request's events as text only. {{member}} is their username. "This" is the request.

topic.request.stream.read.description: Link-style button at the end of the line saying a plan was posted, among the replies on a request's page: opens that plan to read. A verb in the imperative, not the past tense.

topic.run.build.description: Row label in the opened Checks step of a change: the progress of building a preview of the app with the change. A noun.

topic.run.checks.label.description: Row label in the opened Checks step of a change: the progress of the automated checks the app declares, which open its screens and look for what should be there.

topic.run.checks.passed_one.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.checks.passed_other.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.checks.passedFailed_one.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.passedFailed_other.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.progress.description: Progress at the end of the App checks row while the run is going: {{ran}} checks have run out of {{expected}} declared. Both are already formatted; {{expected}} is a question mark when the total is not known.

topic.run.checks.progressFailed_one.description: Progress at the end of the App checks row while the run is going and some checks have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} declared (a question mark when not known), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.progressFailed_other.description: Progress at the end of the App checks row while the run is going and some checks have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} declared (a question mark when not known), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.starting.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row when the checks are about to begin and none has run yet.

topic.run.checks.waitingForSlot.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row while the run is queued behind other runs. A slot is a free place to run.

topic.run.checks.afterBuild.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row while the preview is still being built: the checks will start once the build finishes.

topic.run.checks.didNotRun.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row when no run is going and no check ran, for example because the build failed.

topic.run.unit.label.description: Row label in the opened Checks step of a change: the progress of the project's own automated code tests.

topic.run.unit.cloning.description: Shown at the end of the Unit tests row while the project's code is being copied before the tests can start.

topic.run.unit.installing.description: Shown at the end of the Unit tests row while the code's dependencies are being installed before the tests can start.

topic.run.unit.passed_one.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.unit.passed_other.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.unit.passedFailed_one.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.unit.passedFailed_other.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.unit.progress.description: Progress at the end of the Unit tests row while the tests are running: {{ran}} tests have run out of {{expected}}. Both are already formatted; {{expected}} is an estimate from the last run, written with a leading ~ ("~13,214"), or a question mark when not known.

topic.run.unit.progressFailed_one.description: Progress at the end of the Unit tests row while the tests are running and some have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} (an estimate written with a leading ~, or a question mark), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.unit.progressFailed_other.description: Progress at the end of the Unit tests row while the tests are running and some have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} (an estimate written with a leading ~, or a question mark), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.details.title.description: Heading, and accessible name, of the sheet that opens over a change's page with its technical side: the pull request, the steps to going live with their checks, and the full description.

topic.details.openOnGitHub.description: Link in the Details sheet of a change, beside its pull-request number: opens that pull request on GitHub in a new tab. "Open" is a verb; GitHub is a product name.

topic.details.description.description: Sub-heading in the Details sheet of a change, over the full technical description of the change. A noun.

topic.details.shots.description: Sub-heading in the Details sheet of a change, over the technical record of its before-and-after screenshots: what was captured and what was left out. "Shot" is a noun, short for screenshot.

card.pill.goesLiveIn.description: Status bar on a proposal's card while its approval window counts down: the change will be merged and go live when the time runs out. {{time}} is the time left, already abbreviated, for example ~2h 5m.

card.pill.setAsideIn.description: Status bar on a proposal's card while its rejection window counts down: the proposal was voted down and will be closed without merging when the time runs out. {{time}} is the time left, already abbreviated, for example ~2h 5m.

card.countdown.daysHours.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown, a day or more, shown inside "Goes live in …". {{days}} and {{hours}} are numbers; d and h abbreviate days and hours. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.days.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown when it is a whole number of days. {{days}} is a number; d abbreviates days. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.hoursMinutes.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown, between an hour and a day. {{hours}} and {{minutes}} are numbers; h and m abbreviate hours and minutes. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.hours.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown when it is a whole number of hours. {{hours}} is a number; h abbreviates hours. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.minutes.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown when under an hour. {{minutes}} is a number, at least 1; m abbreviates minutes. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.pill.moreReasons_one.text: and {{count}} more reason, open for details
card.pill.moreReasons_one.description: The whole tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons and the first one has no text to show. {{count}} is how many further reasons there are; "open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Shown alone, in lower case.

card.pill.moreReasons_other.text: and {{count}} more reasons, open for details
card.pill.moreReasons_other.description: The whole tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons and the first one has no text to show. {{count}} is how many further reasons there are; "open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Shown alone, in lower case.

card.pill.reasonAndMore_one.text: {{reason}} · and {{count}} more reason, open for details
card.pill.reasonAndMore_one.description: Tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons: the first reason, then how many more there are. {{reason}} is the first reason, a sentence supplied already worded; {{count}} is how many further reasons there are. "Open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Keep the middle dot, or your language's separator, between the two parts.

card.pill.reasonAndMore_other.text: {{reason}} · and {{count}} more reasons, open for details
card.pill.reasonAndMore_other.description: Tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons: the first reason, then how many more there are. {{reason}} is the first reason, a sentence supplied already worded; {{count}} is how many further reasons there are. "Open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Keep the middle dot, or your language's separator, between the two parts.

card.pill.advisoryVotes_one.text: {{count}} advisory vote from non-approvers, so they don't count toward merging
card.pill.advisoryVotes_one.description: Tooltip on the small +N beside a proposal's vote tally. {{count}} is the number of votes cast by members who are not among the project's approvers; those votes are shown but do not count toward merging the change.

card.pill.advisoryVotes_other.text: {{count}} advisory votes from non-approvers, so they don't count toward merging
card.pill.advisoryVotes_other.description: Tooltip on the small +N beside a proposal's vote tally. {{count}} is the number of votes cast by members who are not among the project's approvers; those votes are shown but do not count toward merging the change.

card.pill.lockFallback.text: This change needs a Yes from another member. It won’t merge on a timer: it needs real Yes votes to reach the app’s normal threshold.
card.pill.lockFallback.description: Tooltip on the lock mark of a proposal card's status bar, used when the server gave no reason of its own. "Change" is the proposal (a noun); "Yes" is a Yes vote.

card.preview.open.description: Accessible name of the Preview button on a proposal's card: opens a running preview build of the proposed change. "Open" is a verb.

card.preview.label.description: Visible label of the button on a proposal's card that opens a running preview build of the proposed change. A noun: the preview.

card.preview.building.description: Label of the disabled Preview button on a proposal's card while the preview of the change is still being built. "Building" is the verb in progress.

card.preview.buildingName.description: Accessible name of the spinner shown in place of the Preview button on a compact card while the preview of the change is still being built.

card.preview.unavailable.description: Badge on a proposal's card, where the Preview button would be, when the preview of the change could not be built.

card.preview.unavailableName.description: Accessible name of the crossed-out eye icon on a compact card when the preview of the change could not be built.

card.badge.threadMessages.description: Tooltip on the speech-bubble count on a card: the number beside it counts the messages in that proposal's or request's discussion thread.

card.vote.sheet.approve.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for a change on a project that is just yours: approves the change so it goes live. "Approve" is a verb. Keep the check mark and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.dontApprove.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for a change on a project that is just yours: declines to approve the change. Keep the cross and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.yes.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for voting on a proposal: votes Yes. Keep the check mark and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.yesTally.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for voting on a proposal: votes Yes. {{tally}} is where the Yes side stands, for example 2/3 (votes so far of votes needed). Keep the check mark and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.stillYes.description: Row in the phone's action sheet when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: repeats their Yes on the new version. Keep the check mark and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.stillYesTally.description: Row in the phone's action sheet when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: repeats their Yes on the new version. {{tally}} is where the Yes side stands, for example 2/3. Keep the check mark and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.no.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for voting on a proposal: votes No. Keep the cross and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.noTally.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for voting on a proposal: votes No. {{tally}} is where the No side stands, for example 1/3. Keep the cross and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.notThisTime.description: Row in the phone's action sheet when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: votes No on the new version. Keep the cross and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.notThisTimeTally.description: Row in the phone's action sheet when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: votes No on the new version. {{tally}} is where the No side stands, for example 1/3. Keep the cross and the two spaces first.

card.vote.face.approved.description: Label of the approval button on a card once the person has approved the change on a project that is just theirs. A settled state, not an action.
