card.vote.face.notApproved.description: Label of the approval button on a card after the person declined to approve the change on a project that is just theirs. Pressing it lets them change that.

card.vote.face.approve.description: Label of the button on a card of a change on a project that is just the person's: opens the picker where they approve it or not. A verb.

card.vote.face.yes.description: Label of the vote button on a card after the person voted Yes on the proposal or request. It shows their current vote; a check mark is drawn before it.

card.vote.face.no.description: Label of the vote button on a card after the person voted No on the proposal or request. It shows their current vote; a cross is drawn before it.

card.vote.face.stillYes.description: Label of the vote button on a card when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal and has not voted on the new one. It asks whether their Yes still stands.

card.vote.face.vote.description: Label of the vote button on a proposal's or request's card before the person has voted: opens the picker with Yes and No. A verb.

card.vote.title.sending.description: Tooltip on a card's vote button while the person's vote is being sent to the server.

card.vote.title.approved.description: Tooltip on the approval button of a change the person has already approved on a project that is just theirs. "It" is the change.

card.vote.title.notApproved.text: You didn’t approve it. Press to change that.
card.vote.title.notApproved.description: Tooltip on the approval button after the person declined to approve a change on a project that is just theirs. "It" is the change.

card.vote.title.approve.text: Approve it, and it goes live.
card.vote.title.approve.description: Tooltip on the Approve button of a change on a project that is just the person's: their approval merges the change and puts it live. "It" is the change.

card.vote.title.votedYes.text: You voted Yes. Press to change your vote.
card.vote.title.votedYes.description: Tooltip on a card's vote button after the person voted Yes on the proposal or request.

card.vote.title.votedNo.text: You voted No. Press to change your vote.
card.vote.title.votedNo.description: Tooltip on a card's vote button after the person voted No on the proposal or request.

card.vote.title.priorYes.text: You said yes to an earlier version. One tap carries it onto this one.
card.vote.title.priorYes.description: Tooltip on a card's "Still yes?" button: the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal, and one press repeats that vote on the current version.

card.vote.title.cast.description: Tooltip on a card's Vote button before the person has voted. {{yesTally}} and {{noTally}} are where each side stands, for example 2/3 (votes so far of votes needed); either may be empty.

card.vote.sending.description: Label that replaces a card's vote button text while the person's vote is being sent.

card.vote.dialog.approval.description: Accessible name of the picker that opens from the Approve button on a card, on a project that is just the person's. A noun: the approval they give or withhold.

card.vote.dialog.vote.description: Accessible name of the picker that opens from a card's Vote button. A noun: the vote the person casts.

card.vote.picker.headApproval.description: Heading inside the picker over its two choices, Approve and Don't approve, on a project that is just the person's. A noun.

card.vote.picker.headVote.description: Heading inside the vote picker over its two choices, Yes and No. A noun.

card.vote.picker.uncounted.text: Test account: this vote won’t count.
card.vote.picker.uncounted.description: Note inside the vote picker shown to a test account voting on a project a real person made: the vote is recorded and shown but not counted.

card.vote.picker.advisory.text: Your vote is advisory: it’s recorded, but it doesn’t decide this change.
card.vote.picker.advisory.description: Note inside the vote picker shown to someone outside the people who decide on this project — not an approver where only approvers decide, or outside every group the project’s rules name. Their vote is recorded and shown, but does not affect the outcome.

card.vote.picker.approve.description: First of the two choices in the picker on a project that is just the person's: approve the change. A verb.

card.vote.picker.dontApprove.description: Second of the two choices in the picker on a project that is just the person's: do not approve the change.

card.vote.picker.yes.description: First of the two choices in the vote picker: a Yes vote on the proposal or request. The side's tally is drawn after it.

card.vote.picker.no.description: Second of the two choices in the vote picker: a No vote on the proposal or request. The side's tally is drawn after it.

card.vote.picker.stillYes.description: First of the two choices in the vote picker when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: keep that Yes on the new version.

card.vote.picker.notThisTime.description: Second of the two choices in the vote picker when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: vote No on the new version.

card.vote.picker.noteLabel.text: Add a note, if you like.
card.vote.picker.noteLabel.description: Label over the optional text box in the picker when the Yes or Approve side is chosen on a project that is just the person's, so there is no group to address.

card.vote.picker.lineLabel.text: Add a line for the group, if you like.
card.vote.picker.lineLabel.description: Label over the optional text box in the vote picker when Yes is chosen: one line of comment that the community's other members will see with the vote.

card.vote.picker.noLabel.text: What’s not working for you? One line is plenty.
card.vote.picker.noLabel.description: Label over the text box in the vote picker when No (or Don't approve) is chosen. A reason is required for a No; one short line is enough.

card.vote.picker.yesPlaceholder.text: What do you like about it?
card.vote.picker.yesPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the vote picker's text box when Yes is chosen. "It" is the proposed change.

card.vote.picker.noPlaceholder.text: What would you want to change?
card.vote.picker.noPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the vote picker's text box when No is chosen. "Change" is a verb: what the person would alter about the proposal.

card.vote.picker.sendYes.description: Button at the bottom of the vote picker when Yes is chosen: sends a Yes vote. "Vote" is a verb.

card.vote.picker.sendNo.description: Button at the bottom of the vote picker when No is chosen: sends a No vote. "Vote" is a verb.

card.vote.picker.sendApprove.description: Button at the bottom of the picker on a project that is just the person's, when Approve is chosen: sends the approval. A verb.

card.vote.picker.sendDontApprove.description: Button at the bottom of the picker on a project that is just the person's, when Don't approve is chosen: sends the refusal with its reason.

card.explore.unavailable.text: AI chat isn't configured on this deployment.
card.explore.unavailable.description: Tooltip on the disabled "Explore in a coding agent" button on a card when this Homeroom installation has no AI model set up.

card.explore.label.description: Button on a proposal's card, after a sparkles emoji: opens a chat with a coding agent about this proposal so the person can ask about or try the change. "Explore" is a verb.

card.menu.more.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the menu button at the end of a card's row of actions: opens the rest of that proposal's or request's actions.

card.title.proposalInput.description: Accessible name of the text field that edits a proposal's title in place. A proposal is a change put up for a vote.

card.title.requestInput.description: Accessible name of the text field that edits a request's title in place. A request is a filed issue asking for a change; "request" is a noun.

card.title.editProposal.description: Tooltip on the pencil beside a proposal's title, shown to its author: starts editing the title.

card.title.editRequest.text: Edit this request's title (you asked for it)
card.title.editRequest.description: Tooltip on the pencil beside a request's title, shown to the person who filed the request. "You asked for it" means they are its author; "request" is a noun.

card.title.edit.description: Accessible name of the pencil button beside a proposal's or request's title: starts editing the title. "Edit" is a verb.

card.illustration.altProposed.description: Alternative text of the image on a card that proposes a new featured illustration for the project: the illustration being proposed. The featured illustration is the picture on the project's Discover card.

card.illustration.altCurrent.description: Alternative text of the image on a card that proposes a new featured illustration for the project: the illustration in use now. The featured illustration is the picture on the project's Discover card.

card.illustration.removed.text: Removed, the app icon shows instead
card.illustration.removed.description: Shown in place of the proposed image on a card whose proposal is to take the project's featured illustration down: with none, the app's icon is shown on its Discover card.

card.illustration.none.text: No illustration, the app icon shows
card.illustration.none.description: Shown in place of an image on a featured-illustration proposal's card when that side (current or proposed) has no illustration: the app's icon is shown on its Discover card instead.

card.illustration.current.description: Small caption over the left thumbnail on a featured-illustration proposal's card: the illustration in use now.

card.illustration.proposed.description: Small caption over the right thumbnail on a featured-illustration proposal's card: the illustration the proposal would put in its place.

card.claims.label.description: Label before the list of members who have claimed a request (said they are working on it), shown to admins on the request's page. A plural noun; keep the colon.

card.claims.release.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the × beside a member's name in a request's claim list: an admin removes that member's claim on the request. {{username}} is the member's username. "Release" is a verb.

kanban.sort.priority.description: Label of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while proposals are ordered by how much they need this person's vote. Names the current order.

kanban.sort.newest.description: Label of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while proposals are ordered newest first. Names the current order.

kanban.sort.namePriority.text: Sort Waiting for approval: Vote priority. Switch to Newest.
kanban.sort.namePriority.description: Accessible name of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while it is sorted by vote priority; pressing it switches to newest first. "Waiting for approval" is the column's name; "Sort" is a verb.

kanban.sort.nameNewest.text: Sort Waiting for approval: Newest. Switch to Vote priority.
kanban.sort.nameNewest.description: Accessible name of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while it is sorted newest first; pressing it switches to vote priority. "Waiting for approval" is the column's name; "Sort" is a verb.

kanban.sort.titlePriority.text: Unvoted first, then fewest qualifying votes still needed. Within each vote group, already-qualified proposals follow those still short. Newest breaks ties. Click to switch to Newest.
kanban.sort.titlePriority.description: Tooltip of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while it is sorted by vote priority: explains the order (proposals this person has not voted on first, then those closest to enough votes) and that a click switches to newest first.

kanban.sort.titleNewest.text: Most recently submitted for review first. Click to switch to Vote priority.
kanban.sort.titleNewest.description: Tooltip of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while it is sorted newest first: explains the order and that a click switches to vote priority.

kanban.column.loading.description: Read by a screen reader while one column of a project's board is loading. {{column}} is the column's name, for example Requests or Done.

kanban.tabs.name.description: Accessible name of the row of steps over a project's board (Requests, Underway, Waiting for approval, Done, each with its count): the heads of the board's columns, and on a phone the tabs that switch between them. The board is a project's kanban of requests and proposals.

kanban.skeleton.requests.description: Name of the board's first column in its loading placeholder: filed requests (issues) nobody has started on. A plural noun.

kanban.skeleton.underway.description: Name of the board's second column in its loading placeholder: work somebody is building now.

kanban.skeleton.waiting.description: Name of the board's third column in its loading placeholder: proposals put up for a vote and not yet approved.

kanban.skeleton.done.description: Name of the board's last column in its loading placeholder: changes that were merged. Not a button.

kanban.skeleton.loadingBoard.description: Read by a screen reader while a project's board (its kanban of requests and proposals) is loading.

kanban.skeleton.loading.description: Read by a screen reader while a list of cards on a project's page is loading.

kanban.footer.showAll_one.description: Last line at the foot of the board's Done column, which hides older merged changes: pressing it shows every one. {{number}} is how many merged changes there are in all, already formatted with digit separators.

kanban.footer.showAll_other.description: Last line at the foot of the board's Done column, which hides older merged changes: pressing it shows every one. {{number}} is how many merged changes there are in all, already formatted with digit separators.

kanban.footer.loading.description: The "Show more" line at the foot of the board's Done column while the next page of merged changes is being fetched.

kanban.footer.loadMoreCount_one.description: Last line at the foot of the board's Done column: pressing it fetches and shows the next merged changes. {{number}} is how many more there are, already formatted with digit separators.

kanban.footer.loadMoreCount_other.description: Last line at the foot of the board's Done column: pressing it fetches and shows the next merged changes. {{number}} is how many more there are, already formatted with digit separators.

kanban.footer.loadMore.description: Last line at the foot of the board's Done column when the number left is unknown: pressing it fetches and shows the next merged changes.

kanban.footer.moreRequests.description: Link under the board's Requests column: opens the rest of the project's open requests (issues) on GitHub. Keep the arrow last.

kanban.footer.moreCompleted_one.description: Note under a board column: {{count}} further completed items are not listed. Keep the leading +.

kanban.footer.moreCompleted_other.description: Note under a board column: {{count}} further completed items are not listed. Keep the leading +.

kanban.archived.show_one.description: Toggle at the end of a column of the person's coding sessions: unfolds the list of sessions they archived. {{count}} is how many are archived.

kanban.archived.show_other.description: Toggle at the end of a column of the person's coding sessions: unfolds the list of sessions they archived. {{count}} is how many are archived.

kanban.archived.state.description: Second line of a row in the archived-sessions list: says the coding session is archived. A state, not a button.

kanban.archived.restoreTitle.description: Tooltip on the Unarchive button of an archived coding session: restoring it also reopens its pull request (PR) on GitHub.

kanban.archived.unarchive.description: Button on a row of the archived-sessions list: restores that coding session. A verb.

card.fold.fold.description: Accessible name of the mark at the top right of an open card: collapses the card back to its one-row form. "Fold" is a verb.

card.fold.new.description: Small lower-case marker after an item's title in a project's lists: the item arrived or changed since the person's last visit.

card.fold.placing.description: Small lower-case marker after an item's title on the Workshop tab while Homeroom is still sorting the item into one of the project's themes.

card.fold.placingTitle.description: Tooltip on the "placing…" marker after an item's title: Homeroom is still sorting the item into a theme.

card.fold.openCard.description: Link button on an unfolded card: goes to that proposal's or request's own page. "Open" is a verb.

card.fold.openSession.description: Link under an unfolded card about the person's own coding session: goes to that session's chat. "Open" is a verb; keep the › last.

feedThread.reply.placeholder.description: Placeholder of the reply box under an open card: the person writes a reply in that proposal's or request's discussion thread. A verb.

feedThread.reply.name.description: Accessible name of the reply box under an open card. The item is the proposal or request the card is about.

feedThread.reply.send.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the round arrow button beside the reply box under an open card: posts the reply.

feedThread.earlier_one.description: Line above the replies shown under an open card: {{count}} older replies in the thread are not shown here.

feedThread.earlier_other.description: Line above the replies shown under an open card: {{count}} older replies in the thread are not shown here.

feedThread.postFailed.text: That didn’t send. Try again, or open the item to reply there.
feedThread.postFailed.description: Error under an open card when posting a reply failed. "Open the item" means go to the proposal's or request's own page.

feedThread.unknownAuthor.description: Stands where an author's username is shown beside a reply in the short thread preview under a card, when the author is not known. Shown alone in the name's own element; lower case in English, like a username.

typeahead.mention.name.description: Accessible name of the list of people that opens when the person types @ in a reply box under a card: picking one inserts that member's @name.

typeahead.ref.name.text: Insert a pull request or issue reference
typeahead.ref.name.description: Accessible name of the list that opens when the person types # or PR# in a reply box under a card: picking a row inserts that pull request's or issue's number.

menu.button.remix.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the round ⋯ button on a project's page, for a visitor who can only read the project. Its menu then holds one action, Remix, which makes the person their own copy of the project.

menu.button.manage.text: Suggest an improvement, import a PR or manage this app
menu.button.manage.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the round ⋯ button on a project's page, for someone who can take part. It opens the project's menu of actions and settings. PR is a GitHub pull request.

menu.suggest.title.description: First, highlighted row of a project's ⋯ menu. Opens the form for describing a problem or an idea for this project, without building it.

menu.suggest.sub.text: Report a problem or idea without building it yourself
menu.suggest.sub.description: Second line of the 'Suggest an improvement' row in a project's ⋯ menu, explaining what the row is for.

menu.build.title.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu: starts a new change to the project that the person builds themselves with a coding agent. 'Build' is a verb; 'it' is the improvement they have in mind.

menu.build.sub.text: With a coding agent, then ask for approval
menu.build.sub.description: Second line of the 'Build it now' row in a project's ⋯ menu: the person works with an AI coding agent, then puts the result up for the community's approval.

menu.importPr.title.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu, shown to people who may build the project: brings in a feature that already exists as a GitHub pull request (PR), so it becomes a proposal here.

menu.importPr.sub.text: Your computer · your own tools. You have already built it, so there is no chat for this one
menu.importPr.sub.description: Second line of the 'Import Feature from a PR' row in a project's ⋯ menu. It says the work was done on the person's own machine with their own tools, so no coding-agent chat is opened. Keep the middle dot between the first two phrases.

menu.settings.title.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu that opens the group of the project's settings and its approval rules. It has a chevron beside it.

menu.settings.heading.description: Heading at the top of the settings panel inside a project's ⋯ menu, beside a back chevron. Pressing it returns to the menu's first list.

menu.settings.back.description: Accessible name of the heading button at the top of the settings panel in a project's ⋯ menu: returns from the settings rows to the menu's first list.

menu.leave.named.description: Row among a project's settings for a member who did not start it: the person stops being a member of this community. 'Leave' is a verb. {{project}} is the project's name.

menu.leave.plain.description: Row among a project's settings for a member who did not start it, when the project's name is not known: the person stops being a member of this community. A verb.

menu.appSettings.title.description: Row among a project's settings, shown to those who manage it: opens the dialog for who can use and build the app, and for deleting it.

menu.appSettings.sub.text: Manage who can use and build this app
menu.appSettings.sub.description: Second line of the 'App settings' row in a project's settings. 'Build' is a verb, to work on the app's code.

menu.domain.title.description: Row among a project's settings, for the people who manage it: opens the dialog for giving the project a web address of its own, beside its Homeroom address.

menu.domain.sub.text: Use your own web address for this project
menu.domain.sub.description: Second line of the 'Custom domain' row in a project's settings.

menu.illustration.title.description: Row among a project's settings, shown to those who may edit it: opens the editor for the picture shown on the project's card on the Discover screen.

menu.illustration.sub.text: Preview and adjust the Discover card image
menu.illustration.sub.description: Second line of the 'Featured illustration' row in a project's settings. Discover is the name of the screen for finding apps and communities.

menu.approvals.title.description: Row among the settings of Homeroom's own project (the platform itself): opens the dialog that sets who approves proposals, changes put up for a vote, and how many approvals one needs.

menu.approvals.sub.text: Who approves proposals and how many approvals are needed
menu.approvals.sub.description: Second line of the 'Proposal approvals' row in the platform project's settings. A proposal is a change put up for a vote.

menu.members.title.description: Row among a project's settings: opens the dialog listing the project's collaborators and admins and the rule for approving proposals.

menu.members.sub.text: Manage collaborators, app admins and proposal approvals
menu.members.sub.description: Second line of the 'Members & approvals' row in a project's settings. Collaborators are people allowed to build the project; a proposal is a change put up for a vote.

menu.rename.title.description: Row among a project's settings: opens the dialog for proposing a new name for the app, the name people see.

menu.rename.sub.text: Renames are proposals, applied once voted in
menu.rename.sub.description: Second line of the 'App display name' row in a project's settings: a new name is itself a change put up for a vote, and takes effect only when the vote passes.

menu.secrets.appTitle.description: Row among a project's settings: opens the dialog for the app's secret values, such as API keys its server reads. A short status may follow this title.

menu.secrets.appSub.description: Second line of the 'App secrets' row in a project's settings.

menu.secrets.platformTitle.description: Row among the settings of Homeroom's own project (the platform itself), in place of 'App secrets': opens the dialog for the platform's environment variables. A short status may follow this title.

menu.secrets.platformSub.text: The platform's own env, applied on its next deploy
menu.secrets.platformSub.description: Second line of the 'Platform variables' row. 'env' is the developers' short word for environment variables; the values take effect the next time the platform is deployed.

menu.suggestBack.title.description: Row among a project's settings, shown to the owner of a remix (a copy of another project): sends the copy's changes to the project it was copied from, as a proposal there. 'This' is the copy's changes.

menu.suggestBack.sub.text: Send your changes to {{project}} as a proposal
menu.suggestBack.sub.description: Second line of the 'Suggest this back' row. {{project}} is the name of the project this one was copied from. A proposal is a change put up for a vote.

menu.remix.title.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu: makes the person their own copy of this project to change freely. A verb here.

menu.remix.sub.description: Second line of the 'Remix' row in a project's ⋯ menu, saying what remixing does.

attr.assignee.removeHint.text: Click again to remove your pick
attr.assignee.removeHint.description: Tooltip on a person's row in the assignee picker of a request or proposal, shown on the person the viewer already picked: clicking the row again withdraws that pick.

attr.add.description: Button beside the text box at the bottom of the category or assignee picker of a request or proposal: adds what was typed as the viewer's pick.

attr.loadFailed.description: Shown inside the priority, category or assignee picker of a request or proposal when its list of options could not be fetched.

board.discussion.open.description: Tooltip of the 'General discussion' card above a project's board: the card opens the project's shared chat channel. 'Open' is a verb.

board.discussion.title.description: Title of the card above a project's board that leads to the project's shared chat channel. The last message said there is shown under it.

pause.resume.description: Button on the amber 'merges are paused' banner of a project, shown to an admin: lets approved proposals merge again although the main branch's tests are failing.

pause.resumeHint.text: Resume merges on this app while main’s unit suite is red. The pause returns if a later merge fails the suite again.
pause.resumeHint.description: Tooltip of the 'Resume merges' button on a project's 'merges are paused' banner. 'main' is the name of the main code branch and stays as it is; its unit suite is the automated tests; 'red' means failing.

pause.confirming.plain.text: Main’s unit suite failed once. Re-running to confirm. Merges are paused meanwhile, except for proposals already level with main whose own checks passed.
pause.confirming.plain.description: Amber banner on a project's page after the automated tests of the main code branch failed for the first time and are being run again. 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is. A proposal 'level with main' already contains everything on that branch.

pause.confirming.since.text: Main’s unit suite failed once since {{commit}}. Re-running to confirm. Merges are paused meanwhile, except for proposals already level with main whose own checks passed.
pause.confirming.since.description: Amber banner on a project's page after the automated tests of the main code branch failed for the first time and are being run again. {{commit}} is the short code of the commit that broke them. 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is.

pause.confirming.test.text: Main’s unit suite failed once: {{test}}. Re-running to confirm. Merges are paused meanwhile, except for proposals already level with main whose own checks passed.
pause.confirming.test.description: Amber banner on a project's page after the automated tests of the main code branch failed for the first time and are being run again. {{test}} is the name of the first failing test, as the test run printed it. 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is.

pause.confirming.sinceTest.text: Main’s unit suite failed once since {{commit}}: {{test}}. Re-running to confirm. Merges are paused meanwhile, except for proposals already level with main whose own checks passed.
pause.confirming.sinceTest.description: Amber banner on a project's page after the automated tests of the main code branch failed for the first time and are being run again. {{commit}} is the short code of the commit that broke them and {{test}} the name of the first failing test. 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is.

pause.paused.plain.text: Merges are paused: main’s unit suite is failing. They resume when a fix lands or an admin resumes them; a proposal already level with main whose own checks passed still merges.
pause.paused.plain.description: Amber banner on a project's page while the automated tests of the main code branch are failing, so approved proposals are not merged. 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is. A proposal 'level with main' already contains everything on that branch.

pause.paused.since.text: Merges are paused: main’s unit suite is failing since {{commit}}. They resume when a fix lands or an admin resumes them; a proposal already level with main whose own checks passed still merges.
pause.paused.since.description: Amber banner on a project's page while the automated tests of the main code branch are failing, so approved proposals are not merged. {{commit}} is the short code of the commit that broke them. 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is.

pause.paused.test.text: Merges are paused: main’s unit suite is failing: {{test}}. They resume when a fix lands or an admin resumes them; a proposal already level with main whose own checks passed still merges.
pause.paused.test.description: Amber banner on a project's page while the automated tests of the main code branch are failing, so approved proposals are not merged. {{test}} is the name of the first failing test, as the test run printed it. 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is.

pause.paused.sinceTest.text: Merges are paused: main’s unit suite is failing since {{commit}}: {{test}}. They resume when a fix lands or an admin resumes them; a proposal already level with main whose own checks passed still merges.
pause.paused.sinceTest.description: Amber banner on a project's page while the automated tests of the main code branch are failing, so approved proposals are not merged. {{commit}} is the short code of the commit that broke them and {{test}} the name of the first failing test. 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.openRun.description: Link at the end of the amber 'merged but not released' banner on the platform project's page: opens, on GitHub, the run of the release workflow the banner is about. 'Open' is a verb; 'run' is a noun.

releaseStall.failed.prCommit.text: PR #{{pr}} ({{commit}}) merged but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.prCommit.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change is not live because the automated release job failed. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number and {{commit}} the merged commit's short code. 'Run it' means run the release workflow; 'main' is the main branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.failed.prCommitRunning.text: PR #{{pr}} ({{commit}}) merged but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. The platform is still running {{running}}. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.prCommitRunning.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change is not live because the automated release job failed. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number, {{commit}} the merged commit's short code and {{running}} the short code of the build still being served. 'Run it' means run the release workflow; 'main' is the main branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.failed.pr.text: PR #{{pr}} merged but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.pr.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change is not live because the automated release job failed. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number. 'Run it' means run the release workflow; 'main' is the main branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.failed.prRunning.text: PR #{{pr}} merged but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. The platform is still running {{running}}. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.prRunning.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change is not live because the automated release job failed. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number and {{running}} the short code of the build still being served. 'Run it' means run the release workflow; 'main' is the main branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.failed.commit.text: Commit {{commit}} landed on main but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.commit.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a commit pushed straight to the main branch is not live because the automated release job failed. {{commit}} is the commit's short code, or the word for unknown in parentheses. 'Run it' means run the release workflow; 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.failed.commitUnknown.text: Commit (unknown) landed on main but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.commitUnknown.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a commit pushed straight to the main branch is not live because the automated release job failed. Used when the commit is not known; "(unknown)" is written as the banner has always shown it.

releaseStall.failed.commitRunning.text: Commit {{commit}} landed on main but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. The platform is still running {{running}}. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.commitRunning.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a commit pushed straight to the main branch is not live because the automated release job failed. {{commit}} is the commit's short code, or the word for unknown in parentheses; {{running}} is the short code of the build still being served. 'Run it' means run the release workflow; 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.failed.commitUnknownRunning.text: Commit (unknown) landed on main but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. The platform is still running {{running}}. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.

clamp.showMore.description: Button under a long comment that is cut off after four lines, on a request's or proposal's card and page: shows the whole comment.

clamp.showLess.description: Button under a long comment that has been expanded, on a request's or proposal's card and page: cuts it back to four lines.

filters.quick.assignedToYou.description: Toggle chip in the filter strip above a project's list of requests and proposals: shows only the items assigned to the viewer.

filters.quick.createdByYou.description: Toggle chip in the filter strip above a project's list of requests and proposals: shows only the items the viewer started.

filters.search.placeholder.description: Placeholder of the search box above a project's list of requests and changes (proposals). The search also reads their comments; '#' means an item's number can be typed.

filters.search.label.description: Accessible name of the search box above a project's list of requests and proposals; typing narrows the list. 'Filter' is a verb.

filters.button.hint.description: Tooltip of the 'Filters' chip above a project's list of requests and proposals: opens the dialog with every filter. 'Filter' is a verb; the board is that list.

filters.button.none.description: Chip beside the search box above a project's list of requests and proposals, while no filter is on: opens the filters dialog. A plural noun.

filters.button.active_one.description: Chip beside the search box above a project's list of requests and proposals while filters are on: opens the filters dialog. {{count}} is how many filters are on.

filters.button.active_other.description: Chip beside the search box above a project's list of requests and proposals while filters are on: opens the filters dialog. {{count}} is how many filters are on.

filters.chip.remove.description: Accessible name of the chip for one active filter above a project's list of requests and proposals; pressing the chip turns that filter off. {{filter}} is the chip's own label, for example a category or a person.

suggestBack.title.description: Title and accessible name of the dialog a remix's owner opens to send the copy's changes to the project it was copied from. {{project}} is that original project's name.

suggestBack.intro.text: Your changes since you remixed go to {{project}} as a proposal. Its members try it and vote, like any other change.
suggestBack.intro.description: Explanation at the top of the 'Suggest this back' dialog. {{project}} is the name of the project the person's copy was made from; a proposal is a change put up for its members' vote.

suggestBack.loading.description: Shown in the box of the 'Suggest this back' dialog while the list of the copy's changes is being fetched.

suggestBack.changes.none.description: Shown in the box of the 'Suggest this back' dialog when there is no change to list for the person's copy.

suggestBack.changes.more_one.description: The whole last line of the list of changes in the 'Suggest this back' dialog. Each line of that list is its own element, one change per line; this final line stands for the changes that are not listed. {{count}} is how many those are.

suggestBack.changes.more_other.description: The whole last line of the list of changes in the 'Suggest this back' dialog. Each line of that list is its own element, one change per line; this final line stands for the changes that are not listed. {{count}} is how many those are.

suggestBack.changes.files_one.description: The only line of the list of changes in the 'Suggest this back' dialog when the changes have no descriptions: how many files of the project differ.

suggestBack.changes.files_other.description: The only line of the list of changes in the 'Suggest this back' dialog when the changes have no descriptions: how many files of the project differ.

suggestBack.notSent.text: Not sent: {{copy}}’s name, who can see it, its admins or its data.
suggestBack.notSent.description: Small note in the 'Suggest this back' dialog listing what stays with the person's copy and is not part of what is sent. {{copy}} is the copy's own name.

suggestBack.openOriginal.description: Link in the 'Suggest this back' dialog, after the server's sentence saying the person must first be let into the original project: goes to that project's page. 'Open' is a verb; {{project}} is its name.

suggestBack.openProposal.description: Link in the 'Suggest this back' dialog, after the server's sentence saying these changes were already sent: goes to that existing proposal. 'Open' is a verb.

suggestBack.sent.text: Sent. Your changes are a proposal on {{project}} now. <0>Open the proposal</0>
suggestBack.sent.description: Confirmation that replaces the 'Suggest this back' dialog's content once the changes were sent. {{project}} is the original project's name; the tagged words link to the new proposal there. 'Open' is a verb.

suggestBack.send.description: Main button of the 'Suggest this back' dialog: sends the copy's changes to the original project as a proposal. {{project}} is that project's name.

suggestBack.sending.description: Label of the 'Suggest this back' dialog's main button while the changes are being sent.

suggestBack.error.loadRetry.text: Could not load your changes. Close this and try again.
suggestBack.error.loadRetry.description: Error in the 'Suggest this back' dialog when the server refused the request for the list of changes without giving its own reason. 'This' is the dialog.

suggestBack.error.load.description: Error in the 'Suggest this back' dialog when fetching the list of changes failed in an unexpected way.

suggestBack.error.notSent.text: Your changes were not sent. Try again.
suggestBack.error.notSent.description: Error in the 'Suggest this back' dialog when the server refused to send the changes without giving its own reason.

suggestBack.error.network.description: Error in the 'Suggest this back' dialog when the request to send the changes could not reach the server.

votingHelp.title.description: Heading of the help popover opened from the ? beside a proposal's votes. It explains how a proposal, a change put up for a vote, gets approved and merged into the app.

votingHelp.liveTitle.description: Small heading in the voting help popover, above one sentence describing where the proposal in view stands at this moment.

votingHelp.rule.voters.text: Only people who’ve actually used the app recently count as voters. The number of Yes votes needed scales with how many active testers there are.
votingHelp.rule.voters.description: First rule in the voting help popover. 'Yes' is the name of the approving vote; 'active testers' are the people who used the app recently.

votingHelp.rule.quiet.text: A proposal with clear support and no objections goes live on its own after a short visibility window (a few days), so everyone has a chance to look. <0>Quiet is taken as a nod</0>, so speak up if something bothers you.
votingHelp.rule.quiet.description: Rule in the voting help popover: a supported proposal with no No votes merges by itself after a few days. The tagged words are shown in bold; they mean that saying nothing counts as agreement.

votingHelp.rule.support.text: The more support a proposal has, the shorter the wait. A clear majority merges almost immediately; thin, unopposed support waits longer.
votingHelp.rule.support.description: Rule in the voting help popover: how the waiting time before a proposal merges depends on how many people voted Yes.

votingHelp.rule.no.text: <0>No</0> votes make a proposal harder to pass: they raise the number of Yes votes needed and lengthen the wait.
votingHelp.rule.no.description: Rule in the voting help popover. 'No' and 'Yes' are the names of the two votes; the tagged 'No' is shown in bold.

votingHelp.rule.conversation.text: If enough people vote No, the proposal <0>needs a conversation</0>. The timer turns off and it needs a straight majority of Yes votes to go live, so talk it through.
votingHelp.rule.conversation.description: Rule in the voting help popover: with enough No votes a proposal no longer merges on a timer and needs more Yes than No. The tagged words are shown in bold and name that state.

votingHelp.rule.setAside.text: A proposal with more No than Yes and little support is set aside after a countdown (“Set aside in …”). Nothing is lost: it can come back as a new proposal.
votingHelp.rule.setAside.description: Rule in the voting help popover: an unpopular proposal is closed after a countdown. The words in quotation marks are the countdown label people see on such a proposal, followed by a time.

votingHelp.rule.checks.text: Even after winning the vote, a proposal only merges once its <0>automated checks pass</0> and it’s <1>up to date with the main app</1>. Locked apps also need an admin’s Yes.
votingHelp.rule.checks.description: Rule in the voting help popover: two further conditions for merging, each tagged and shown in bold. 'Locked apps' are apps whose rules require an admin's approving vote.

votingHelp.rule.custom.text: Apps can customize these rules: restricting approvals to <0>invited approvers</0> (everyone else’s votes stay visible but advisory) and/or requiring a fixed <1>“at least N approvals”</1> instead of the timed majority system.
votingHelp.rule.custom.description: Last rule in the voting help popover: an app may set its own approval rules. Both tagged phrases are shown in bold; N stands for a number the app chooses.

modals.generate.title.description: Title of the dialog that asks before an AI agent writes a proposal for a request. {{number}} is the request's issue number. 'Generate' is a verb.

modals.generate.modelLabel.description: Small uppercase label above the name of the AI model that will write the proposal, in the 'Generate proposal' dialog.

modals.generate.changeModel.description: Link beside the chosen AI model in the 'Generate proposal' dialog: opens the list of models to pick another. 'Change' is a verb.

modals.generate.confirm.description: Main button of the 'Generate proposal' dialog: starts the AI agent that writes a proposal for the request. 'Generate' is a verb.

modals.generate.picker.back.description: Accessible name of the back arrow on the model list of the 'Generate proposal' dialog: returns to the dialog's first view without changing the model.

modals.generate.picker.title.description: Title of the model list in the 'Generate proposal' dialog, where the person picks which AI model writes the proposal.

modals.generate.picker.intro.text: Recommended models are shown first. Search only if you need another model.
modals.generate.picker.intro.description: Line under the 'Choose a model' title in the 'Generate proposal' dialog.

modals.generate.picker.ownKey.title.description: Bold first line of a note in the model list, shown when the person pays for AI with their own key for OpenRouter, a service that gives access to many AI models. OpenRouter is a name.

modals.generate.picker.ownKey.body.text: Model availability follows your OpenRouter privacy settings. To exclude providers that may train on your data, review those settings.
modals.generate.picker.ownKey.body.description: Body of the note about using one's own OpenRouter key in the model list. OpenRouter is a name.

modals.generate.picker.ownKey.link.description: Link under the note about using one's own OpenRouter key: opens the privacy settings page on OpenRouter's website.

modals.generate.picker.searchLabel.description: Accessible label of the search box above the list of AI models in the 'Generate proposal' dialog.

modals.generate.picker.searchPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the search box above the list of AI models in the 'Generate proposal' dialog.

modals.generate.picker.listLabel.description: Accessible name of the list of AI models to choose from in the 'Generate proposal' dialog.

modals.generate.picker.noMatches.description: Shown in place of the list of AI models when the search text matches none.

modals.generate.picker.noRecommended.description: Shown in place of the list of AI models when nothing was searched and there is no recommended model to show.

modals.generate.picker.truncated_one.text: Showing the first {{shown}} of {{count}} match. Keep typing to narrow the list.
modals.generate.picker.truncated_one.description: Note under the list of AI models when a search matches more than are shown. {{shown}} is how many are listed and {{count}} how many matched.

modals.generate.picker.truncated_other.text: Showing the first {{shown}} of {{count}} matches. Keep typing to narrow the list.
modals.generate.picker.truncated_other.description: Note under the list of AI models when a search matches more than are shown. {{shown}} is how many are listed and {{count}} how many matched.

modals.generate.picker.useNamed.description: Main button under the list of AI models, and its tooltip: confirms the selected model. {{model}} is that model's name.

modals.generate.picker.use.description: Main button under the list of AI models while no model is selected; it is disabled then.

modals.aiConsent.title.description: Title of the dialog shown when an app asks to make AI requests paid from the person's own AI budget. {{app}} is the app's name.

modals.aiConsent.titleUnnamed.text: Allow This app to use AI?
modals.aiConsent.titleUnnamed.description: Title of the dialog shown when an app asks to make AI requests paid from the person's own AI budget. Used when the app's name is not known; "This app" is written as the dialog has always shown it.

modals.aiConsent.purposeQuote.description: The app's own stated reason for wanting AI, shown in italics under the dialog's title. {{purpose}} is that reason, written by the app's author; only the quotation marks around it are translated.

modals.aiConsent.eligibilityUnavailable.text: Credit eligibility could not be checked. Close this dialog and try again shortly.
modals.aiConsent.eligibilityUnavailable.description: Notice in the 'Allow app to use AI' dialog when Homeroom could not find out whether the person has free AI credit.

modals.aiConsent.noPayer.text: No AI payer is available yet. <0>Connect GitHub or X</0> to unlock $10/day, or <1>add your own Anthropic API key</1>.
modals.aiConsent.noPayer.description: Notice in the 'Allow app to use AI' dialog when nothing can pay for the app's AI requests. The first tagged phrase links to Settings, linked accounts; the second to Settings, API key. GitHub, X and Anthropic are names; keep $10/day as written.

modals.aiConsent.capLabel.text: Daily cap for this app ($ per day)
modals.aiConsent.capLabel.description: Label of the number box in the 'Allow app to use AI' dialog: the most this app may spend on AI per day, in US dollars.

modals.aiConsent.notNow.description: Button in the 'Allow app to use AI' dialog: closes it without giving the app permission.

modals.aiConsent.allow.description: Main button of the 'Allow app to use AI' dialog: gives the app permission with the daily cap entered.

modals.aiConsent.unavailable.description: Label of the disabled main button in the 'Allow app to use AI' dialog while nothing can pay for AI, in place of 'Allow'.

modals.permission.reasonQuote.description: The app's own stated reason for asking a permission, shown in italics in the permission dialog. {{reason}} is written by the app's author; only the quotation marks around it are translated.

modals.permission.notNow.description: Button in the dialog where an app asks for a permission, such as notifications: closes it without granting the permission.

modals.credits.notNow.description: Button under the card offering ways to get more AI credit: closes the card without choosing one.

modals.checks.title.description: Title and accessible name of the dialog showing the results of a proposal's automated checks. 'Checks' is a noun: the tests run against the proposed change.

modals.checks.none.text: No check results have been recorded yet.
modals.checks.none.description: Shown in the 'Proposal checks' dialog when the proposal's automated checks have produced no result so far.

modals.checks.loading.description: Shown in the 'Proposal checks' dialog while the results are being fetched.

modals.checks.loadFailed.description: Error in the 'Proposal checks' dialog when the server refused the request for the results without giving its own reason.

modals.checks.refresh.description: Button in the 'Proposal checks' dialog: fetches the check results again.

modals.checks.rerunning.description: Label of the button that runs a proposal's automated checks again, in the 'Proposal checks' dialog, while that request is in flight.

topic.back.allItems.description: Text of the back chip at the top of a proposal's or request's page when it was opened from the project's All items page (the whole board of requests and proposals under the Workshop tab), which the chip returns to. Shown after a left-pointing chevron.

topic.back.toAllItems.description: Accessible name of the back chip on a proposal's or request's page that was opened from the project's All items page. All items is the whole board of the project's requests and proposals, under its Workshop tab.

topic.change.descriptionFold.description: Label on a change's page that unfolds the change's full written description (its pull-request text), shown in place of the plain-language summary when the change has none. A noun.

topic.change.diagram.failed.text: The author’s diagram could not be drawn.
topic.change.diagram.failed.description: Muted line on a change's page, where the diagram its author attached would lead the page, when that diagram could not be drawn. The author is the person who put the change up.

topic.change.diagram.showSource.description: Label under the line saying a change's diagram could not be drawn: unfolds the diagram's source text as its author wrote it.

communityCard.rule.editName.description: Accessible name of the Edit button beside the Approval rules heading on a project's Workshop tab: opens the Members & approvals dialog at its approvals section, where a change to the rule is proposed and voted on.

communityCard.line.you.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and you approve it.
communityCard.line.you.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, on a project that is just the viewer's.

communityCard.line.anyOf.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and <0></0><1>{{names}}</1> says yes.
communityCard.line.anyOf.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where any one of the named approvers is enough. <0></0> is where their faces go; <1> wraps {{names}}, their account names joined with "or" (for example "evan or snait"), shown bold.

communityCard.line.allOf.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and <0></0><1>{{names}}</1> say yes.
communityCard.line.allOf.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where every named approver has to say yes. <0></0> is where their faces go; <1> wraps {{names}}, their account names joined with "and" (for example "evan and snait"), shown bold.

communityCard.line.approvers.some_one.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} of the {{total}} approvers says yes.
communityCard.line.approvers.some_one.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where some of the project's approvers must say yes. {{count}} is how many, {{total}} how many approvers there are.

communityCard.line.approvers.some_other.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and {{count}} of the {{total}} approvers say yes.
communityCard.line.approvers.some_other.description: Sentence: the approval rule, in one line at the foot of the All items card on the Workshop tab of a project's page, where some of the project's approvers must say yes. {{count}} is how many, {{total}} how many approvers there are.

communityCard.line.approvers.all_one.text: A change goes live when its checks pass and all {{count}} approvers say yes.

communityCard.rule.rules.description: Button at the end of the approval rule's line on the Workshop tab of a project's page, for people who may change the rule: opens the Members & approvals dialog at its approvals section, where a change to the rule is proposed and voted on.

page.title.hub.description: Title of a project's Hub page, the first of its places: who is here and who it is for, its actions, its trend and what needs the person. A noun, the name of the place.

places.tray.name.description: Accessible name of the tray that slides in from the left on a phone and lists a project's places (its Hub, Needs you, Workshop and its channels). {{project}} is the project's name.

allItems.themes.topics.description: Small upper-case heading over a project's topics on the By category view of its All items page. Topics are the categories its members set up, each with a chat channel of its own. A noun.

allItems.themes.other.description: Small upper-case heading on the By category view of a project's All items page, over the categories that are not one of its topics (the ones the members set up, listed above it).

allItems.theme.discuss.description: Link at the foot of a topic's card on the By category view of a project's All items page: opens that topic's chat channel. {{channel}} is the channel's handle, written after its #, for example onboarding. Keep the # before it and the arrow at the end.

topic.change.gate.release.description: The last sentence of the line under the Votes card on the page of a change to Homeroom itself that has merged. {{release}} is a finished sentence saying when the change goes live, for example "Merged; goes live in the next release (about 8 minutes)"; this entry adds only the full stop that ends it.

diagram.kind.rename.description: Small-caps label over a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page) when the diagram shows a rename: an old name, an arrow, the new name.

diagram.kind.flow.description: Small-caps label over a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page) when the diagram shows the steps of something before the change and after it. Keep the arrow.

diagram.kind.changes.description: Small-caps label over a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page) when the diagram lists what the change adds, changes and removes.

diagram.kind.numbers.description: Small-caps label over a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page) when the diagram compares figures before and after the change, with bars.

diagram.kind.mermaid.description: Small-caps label over a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page) when the diagram is a free-form picture its author drew.

diagram.label.description: Accessible name a screen reader reads for a change's diagram. {{kind}} is the diagram's label, for example "Rename" or "What changes"; {{text}} is the diagram said in words, one or more whole sentences.

diagram.source.decision.description: Small line under a diagram on a Needs-you card: the picture was drawn from the facts of a group decision (a rename, a closed request, a secret setting), not by a person.

diagram.source.files.description: Small line under a picture on a Needs-you card: the picture (which parts of the project the change touches) was made from the files the change edits.

diagram.source.author.description: Small line under a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page): the person or agent who made the change supplied this diagram.

diagram.source.authorMermaid.text: Diagram by the change’s author · Mermaid
diagram.source.authorMermaid.description: Small line under a change's diagram (on a Needs-you card and on the change's page): the change's author supplied it, written in Mermaid. Mermaid is the name of the diagram language; keep it and the middle dot.

diagram.flow.before.description: Label at the start of the first row of a "Before → after" diagram: the steps as they are before the change.

diagram.flow.after.description: Label at the start of the second row of a "Before → after" diagram: the steps as they are once the change is in.

diagram.changes.added.description: Word at the start of a row in a "What changes" diagram: the change adds the thing named on the row.

diagram.changes.changed.description: Word at the start of a row in a "What changes" diagram: the change alters the thing named on the row.

diagram.changes.removed.description: Word at the start of a row in a "What changes" diagram: the change removes the thing named on the row.

diagram.text.rename.description: A rename diagram said in words, for a screen reader. {{from}} is the old name and {{to}} the new one, as the change's author wrote them.

diagram.text.renameIn.description: A rename diagram said in words, for a screen reader. {{from}} is the old name and {{to}} the new one; {{places}} lists where the name appears (for example "Project name" or the screens the author named), already joined into a list.

diagram.text.flow.description: A "Before → after" diagram said in words, for a screen reader. {{before}} and {{after}} are each the steps in order, for example "Vote, then Checks, then Closes".

diagram.text.then.description: How the steps of a "Before → after" diagram follow one another when it is said in words for a screen reader. {{first}} is every step so far and {{second}} the next one; each step is the change author's own words.

diagram.text.added.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change adds {{what}}, the thing the change's author named.

diagram.text.addedDetail.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change adds {{what}}, the thing the change's author named; {{detail}} is the author's short note about it.

diagram.text.changed.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change alters {{what}}, the thing the change's author named.

diagram.text.changedDetail.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change alters {{what}}, the thing the change's author named; {{detail}} is a short note about it.

diagram.text.removed.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change removes {{what}}, the thing the change's author named.

diagram.text.removedDetail.description: One row of a "What changes" diagram said in words, for a screen reader: the change removes {{what}}, the thing the change's author named; {{detail}} is a short note about it.

diagram.text.numbers.description: One row of a "Numbers" diagram said in words, for a screen reader. {{label}} is what is measured, as the change's author named it; {{before}} and {{after}} are the figures before and after the change, each with its unit (for example "2.4 s").

diagram.text.sentences.description: How the sentences of a diagram said in words follow one another, for a screen reader (one sentence per row of the diagram). {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next whole sentence. Change only what stands between them.

diagram.text.mermaid.text: A diagram drawn from its author’s text.
diagram.text.mermaid.description: What a screen reader hears for a free-form diagram that the change's author wrote in a diagram language (Mermaid) and that cannot be said in words.

diagram.decision.projectName.description: Where the name changes, shown as a small chip under a group decision's rename diagram (old name → new name) on a Needs-you card: the project's name.

diagram.decision.secretRemoved.description: Note beside the setting's name in a group decision's "What changes" diagram on a Needs-you card, when the decision removes a secret setting (an API key or password the project keeps hidden).

diagram.decision.secretChanged.text: A secret setting, value not shown
diagram.decision.secretChanged.description: Note beside the setting's name in a group decision's "What changes" diagram on a Needs-you card, when the decision sets a secret setting (an API key or password the project keeps hidden); its new value is never shown.

places.list.hub.description: First entry in a project's list of places (beside the page on a wide window, in the tray on a phone): the project's overview, with who is here, what is new and what waits on you. A noun, the name of the place.

places.list.needsYou.description: Second entry in a project's list of places: the feed of decisions waiting on this person (changes to vote on, requests nobody has taken). A count may follow it.

places.list.workshop.description: Third entry in a project's list of places: the build page, listing the work going on, the requests and the changes. A noun, the name of the place.

places.list.channels.description: Small upper-case heading in a project's list of places, over the project's own chat channel (#general).

places.list.topics.description: Small upper-case heading in a project's list of places, over its topics: the categories its members set up, each a chat channel of its own.

places.list.switchCommunity.description: Last entry of a project's list of places in the tray on a phone: opens the list of the person's communities to go to another one.

places.list.name.description: Accessible name of a project's list of places (its Hub, Needs you, Workshop and channels). {{project}} is the project's name.

places.list.nameUnnamed.description: Accessible name of a project's list of places (its Hub, Needs you, Workshop and channels) when the project's name is not known yet.

places.list.filtered.description: Read only by screen readers, right after Workshop in a project's list of places, while a search or filter is narrowing the project's All items page. Keep the parentheses.

places.list.countAloud.description: Read only by screen readers after an entry in a project's list of places that shows a number: says what the number counts. {{phrase}} is that, already worded, for example "29 to vote" or "3 unread". Keep the parentheses.

places.count.toVote_one.description: What the number beside Needs you in a project's list of places counts, read by screen readers: changes waiting for this person's vote. {{count}} is that number.

places.count.toVote_other.description: What the number beside Needs you in a project's list of places counts, read by screen readers: changes waiting for this person's vote. {{count}} is that number.

places.count.unread_one.description: What the number beside a channel in a project's list of places counts, read by screen readers: messages there this person has not read. {{count}} is that number.

places.count.unread_other.description: What the number beside a channel in a project's list of places counts, read by screen readers: messages there this person has not read. {{count}} is that number.

places.bar.hub.description: Title of the bar at the top of a project's page while its Hub (or the plan under it) is on show: names the place you are on. A noun, the name of the place.

places.bar.needsYou.description: Title of the bar at the top of a project's page while its Needs you place is on show: the feed of decisions waiting on this person.

places.bar.workshop.description: Title of the bar at the top of a project's page while its Workshop (or the All items page under it) is on show: names the place you are on. A noun, the name of the place.

places.bar.button.description: Accessible name of the button on the bar at the top of a project's page that opens the list of the project's places (its Hub, Needs you, Workshop and channels). {{project}} is the project's name.

places.bar.buttonUnnamed.description: Accessible name of the button on the bar at the top of a project's page that opens the list of the project's places, when the project's name is not known yet.

places.bar.waitingAloud.description: Read only by screen readers after the name of the places button at the top of a project's page, while something in the project waits for this person (a dot is shown). {{waiting}} is what waits, already worded, for example "29 to vote, 4 unread". Keep the parentheses.

places.bar.toVote_one.description: One thing that waits for this person, read by screen readers on the places button at the top of a project's page: changes waiting for their vote. {{count}} is how many.

places.bar.toVote_other.description: One thing that waits for this person, read by screen readers on the places button at the top of a project's page: changes waiting for their vote. {{count}} is how many.

places.bar.unread_one.description: One thing that waits for this person, read by screen readers on the places button at the top of a project's page: messages in the project's channels they have not read. {{count}} is how many.

places.bar.unread_other.description: One thing that waits for this person, read by screen readers on the places button at the top of a project's page: messages in the project's channels they have not read. {{count}} is how many.

places.mergedCard.text.description: Card in a topic's chat history at the point where another topic was merged into it. {{channel}} is the merged topic's handle, written after its #, for example signup. Keep the # before it.

places.mergedCard.read.description: Link on the card in a topic's chat history that marks where another topic was merged into it: opens the merged topic's old channel, which can still be read. {{channel}} is that topic's handle, written after its #. Keep the # and the arrow.

places.topicHead.mergedInto.description: Line at the top of a topic's chat channel once the topic was merged into another one: its channel can be read but not written in. {{channel}} is the handle of the topic it joined, written after its #. Keep the #.

places.topicHead.mergedIntoLink.description: Line at the top of a topic's chat channel once the topic was merged into another one: its channel can be read but not written in. {{channel}} is the handle of the topic it joined, written after its #; <0></0> makes it a link that opens that topic. Keep the #.

places.topicHead.mergedUnnamed.text: Merged into another topic. Read only.
places.topicHead.mergedUnnamed.description: Line at the top of a topic's chat channel once the topic was merged into another one that cannot be named: its channel can be read but not written in.

places.topicHead.archived.description: Line at the top of a topic's chat channel once the topic was archived: its channel can be read but not written in.

places.topicHead.requests_one.description: Link at the top of a topic's chat channel: opens the project's All items page narrowed to the open requests filed under this topic. {{count}} is how many there are. Keep the arrow.

places.topicHead.requests_other.description: Link at the top of a topic's chat channel: opens the project's All items page narrowed to the open requests filed under this topic. {{count}} is how many there are. Keep the arrow.

places.topicHead.aboutThenRequests.description: Line at the top of a topic's chat channel. {{about}} is what the topic is for, as its members wrote it; <0></0> is a link to the requests filed under it, and {{requests}} its words, already worded, for example "14 requests ›".

places.topicFigures.label.description: Accessible name of the card of numbers at the top of a topic's chat channel, such as how long checks take or how often the bot's answers fail.

places.topicFigures.window_one.description: Small heading over the card of numbers at the top of a topic's chat channel: says the numbers cover the last day. Shown in capitals.

places.topicFigures.window_other.description: Small heading over the card of numbers at the top of a topic's chat channel: says how many days the numbers cover, for example "Last 7 days". {{count}} is that number. Shown in capitals.

places.topicFigures.whatItMeans.description: Accessible name of the small information button beside one number's name at the top of a topic's chat channel: shows a sentence explaining that number. {{label}} is the number's name, for example "Reply time".

places.topicFigures.demo.text: Staging demo figures, not real numbers.
places.topicFigures.demo.description: Small line under the card of numbers at the top of a topic's chat channel, shown only on a test copy of Homeroom: says the numbers are made up for testing.

topic.request.shots.hideComment.description: Small button on the corner of a screenshot in a request, while the comment pinned to the picture is drawn over it: hides the comment.

topic.request.shots.hideComments.description: Small button on the corner of a screenshot in a request, while the several comments pinned to the picture are drawn over it: hides them.

topic.request.shots.showComment.description: Small button on the corner of a screenshot in a request, while the comment pinned to the picture is hidden: draws it over the picture again.

topic.request.shots.showComments.description: Small button on the corner of a screenshot in a request, while the several comments pinned to the picture are hidden: draws them over the picture again.

touches.kicker.description: Small label at the top of the picture a change's card shows when it has no before and after shots: which parts of the project the change touches, drawn from its files.

touches.files.none.description: Beside an area of the project in the "What it touches" picture, when the change touches no file in it.

touches.files.count_one.description: Beside an area of the project in the "What it touches" picture: how many of the change's files are in it.

touches.files.count_other.description: Beside an area of the project in the "What it touches" picture: how many of the change's files are in it.

touches.area.screens.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: the screens people see (its interface code).

touches.area.server.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: its server code.

touches.area.database.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: its database schema and data.

touches.area.tests.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: its automated tests.

touches.area.docs.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: its documentation.

touches.area.other.description: Area of a project in the "What it touches" picture: files that belong to none of the other areas.

touches.area.withFiles.description: One area in the spoken description of the "What it touches" picture. {{area}} is the area's name (Screens, Server…) and {{files}} how many files, for example "Server, 2 files".

touches.areas.pair.description: How the areas are joined in the spoken description of the "What it touches" picture, for example "Server, 2 files; Tests, 1 file". {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next area. Only the punctuation is translated.

touches.label.description: What a screen reader says for the "What it touches" picture on a change's card: the parts of the project the change touches. {{areas}} lists them, for example "Server, 2 files; Tests, 1 file".

touches.labelNothingVisible.description: The spoken description of the "What it touches" picture when the change's author declared that nothing on screen changes. {{said}} is the description that comes first ("What it touches. Server, 2 files.").

touches.footNothingVisible.text: Nothing on screen changes · drawn from the change’s files
touches.footNothingVisible.description: Line under the "What it touches" picture when the change's author declared that nothing on screen changes; it also says the picture was drawn from the change's files.

menu.topics.title.description: Row in a project's + menu that opens its topics: its lasting conversations, each a channel and a category requests are filed under.

menu.topics.sub.text: The project's channels, and the categories requests are filed under
menu.topics.sub.description: Second line of the Topics row in a project's + menu, saying what topics are.

discussion.topic.none.description: Shown on a project's page when a link names a topic channel the project does not have. {{handle}} is the channel's short name, shown after #.

discussion.topic.mergedInto.text: #{{handle}} was merged into #{{into}}. Its history stays here to read.
discussion.topic.mergedInto.description: Notice under a topic channel that was merged into another, in place of the message box. {{handle}} is this channel's short name and {{into}} the one it joined, each shown after #.

discussion.topic.mergedIntoAnother.text: #{{handle}} was merged into another topic. Its history stays here to read.
discussion.topic.mergedIntoAnother.description: Notice under a topic channel that was merged into another one that can no longer be found, in place of the message box. {{handle}} is this channel's short name, shown after #.

discussion.topic.archived.text: #{{handle}} is archived. Its history stays here to read.
discussion.topic.archived.description: Notice under an archived topic channel, in place of the message box. {{handle}} is the channel's short name, shown after #.

discussion.topic.joinToPost.text: Join this community to post here.
discussion.topic.joinToPost.description: Notice under a topic channel for someone who has not joined the project's community, in place of the message box.

discussion.topic.placeholder.description: Placeholder in the message box of a project's topic channel. {{handle}} is the channel's short name, shown after #.
